crossrefs.raw: 林前八6，罗三30，提前二5，申四35，39

refs.text_gb: 在我们却只有一位神，就是父，万物都本于祂，我们也归于祂；并有一位主，就是耶稣基督，万物都是借着祂有的，我们也是借着祂有的。
refs.text_big5: 在我們卻只有一位神，就是父，萬物都本於祂，我們也歸於祂；並有一位主，就是耶穌基督，萬物都是藉著祂有的，我們也是藉著祂有的。
refs.text_en: Yet to us there is one God, the Father, out from whom are all things, and we are unto Him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we are through Him.

refs.text_gb: 神既是一位，祂就要本于信称那受割礼的为义，也要借着信称那未受割礼的为义。
refs.text_big5: 神既是一位，祂就要本於信稱那受割禮的為義，也要藉著信稱那未受割禮的為義。
refs.text_en: If indeed God is one, who will justify the circumcision out of faith and the uncircumcision through faith.

refs.text_gb: 因为只有一位神，在神和人中间，也只有一位中保，就是那人基督耶稣；
refs.text_big5: 因為只有一位神，在神和人中間，也只有一位中保，就是那人基督耶穌；
refs.text_en: For there is one God and one Mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus,

refs.text_gb: 这些显给你看，是要使你知道，唯有耶和华是神，除祂以外，再无别神。
refs.text_big5: 這些顯給你看，是要使你知道，惟有耶和華是神，除祂以外，再無別神。
refs.text_en: You were shown these things that you might know that it is Jehovah who is God; there is no other besides Him.

refs.text_gb: 所以，今日你要知道，也要记在心上，上天下地唯有耶和华是神，除祂以外，再无别神。
refs.text_big5: 所以，今日你要知道，也要記在心上，上天下地惟有耶和華是神，除祂以外，再無別神。
refs.text_en: Know therefore today and bring it to heart that Jehovah is God in heaven above and upon the earth below; there is no other.

verses.text_gb: 纵然有称为[Cra]神的，或在天，或在地，就如那许多的神，许多的主，
verses.text_big5: 縱然有稱為[Cra]神的，或在天，或在地，就如那許多的神，許多的主，
verses.text_en: For even if there are so-called gods, either in heaven or on earth, even as there are many gods and many lords,
verses.text_gb_plain: 纵然有称为神的，或在天，或在地，就如那许多的神，许多的主，
verses.text_big5_plain: 縱然有稱為神的，或在天，或在地，就如那許多的神，許多的主，

refs.text_gb: 他是那敌对、且高抬自己超过一切称为神，或受人敬拜者的，甚至坐在神的殿里，展示自己，说他就是神。
refs.text_big5: 他是那敵對、且高抬自己超過一切稱為神，或受人敬拜者的，甚至坐在神的殿裏，展示自己，說他就是神。
refs.text_en: Who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God or an object of worship, so that he sits in the temple of God, setting himself forth, saying that he is God.

refs.text_gb: 众民的神都属虚无，唯独耶和华造作诸天。
refs.text_big5: 眾民的神都屬虛無，惟獨耶和華造作諸天。
refs.text_en: For all the gods of the peoples are idols, / But Jehovah made the heavens.

refs.text_gb: 他们饮酒，赞美那用金、银、铜、铁、木、石所造的神。
refs.text_big5: 他們飲酒，讚美那用金、銀、銅、鐵、木、石所造的神。
refs.text_en: They drank wine and praised the gods of gold and of silver, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone.

verses.text_gb: 在[Fn1]我们却只有[Fn2][Cra]一位神，就是[Fn3][Crb]父，[Crc]万物都[Fn4]本于祂，我们也归于祂；并有[Fn5][Crd]一位主，就是[Fn6]耶稣基督，万物都是[Cre]借着祂有的，我们也是借着祂有的。
verses.text_big5: 在[Fn1]我們卻只有[Fn2][Cra]一位神，就是[Fn3][Crb]父，[Crc]萬物都[Fn4]本於祂，我們也歸於祂；並有[Fn5][Crd]一位主，就是[Fn6]耶穌基督，萬物都是[Cre]藉著祂有的，我們也是藉著祂有的。
verses.text_en: Yet to us there is one God, the Father, out from whom are all things, and we are unto Him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we are through Him.
verses.text_gb_plain: 在我们却只有一位神，就是父，万物都本于祂，我们也归于祂；并有一位主，就是耶稣基督，万物都是借着祂有的，我们也是借着祂有的。
verses.text_big5_plain: 在我們卻只有一位神，就是父，萬物都本於祂，我們也歸於祂；並有一位主，就是耶穌基督，萬物都是藉著祂有的，我們也是藉著祂有的。

footnotes.zh: 指在基督里的信徒，基督徒。
footnotes.zh_big5: 指在基督裏的信徒，基督徒。
footnotes.en: 8:6 1 us The believers in Christ, the Christians.

footnotes.zh: 与5节“许多的神”相对。我们的神是独一的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 與5節“許多的神”相對。我們的神是獨一的。
footnotes.en: 8:6 2 one In contrast to many gods in v. 5. Our God is uniquely one.

footnotes.zh: 我们神的一种称呼，祂是万物的源头。这种称呼使我们的神与许多假神绝对有别。
footnotes.zh_big5: 我們神的一種稱呼，祂是萬物的源頭。這種稱呼使我們的神與許多假神絕對有別。
footnotes.en: 8:6 3 Father A designation of our God, who is the source of all things. This designation makes our God utterly distinct from the many false gods.

footnotes.zh: 父是万物的源头，因此万物是“本于祂；”但只有我们信徒要转向祂，因此我们是“归于祂。”同样，父所造的万物，是以耶稣基督为凭借而有的；而我们信徒是以主的重生为凭借，使我们转向而归于父。因此，我们和万物都是“借着祂。”
footnotes.en: 8:6 4 through The Father is the source of all things; thus, all things are out from Him. However, only we as believers will turn to Him; hence, we are unto Him. Similarly, all things that the Father created came into being through Jesus Christ as the means, and it is through the means of the Lord's regeneration that we as believers turn to the Father and are unto Him. Hence, both we and all things are through Christ.

footnotes.zh: 与5节“许多的主”相对。我们的主也是独一的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 與5節“許多的主”相對。我們的主也是獨一的。
footnotes.en: 8:6 5 one In contrast to many lords in v. 5. Our Lord also is uniquely one.

footnotes.zh: 我们的主神圣和属人的名称，这使祂与许多的主有别。我们的神，就是父，是万物独一的源头；我们的主，就是耶稣基督，是独一的凭借，万物都是借着祂成的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 我們的主神聖和屬人的名稱，這使祂與許多的主有別。我們的神，就是父，是萬物獨一的源頭；我們的主，就是耶穌基督，是獨一的憑藉，萬物都是藉著祂成的。
footnotes.en: 8:6 6 Jesus The divine and human title of our Lord that distinguishes Him from the many lords. Our God, the Father, is the unique source of all things, and our Lord, Jesus Christ, is the unique means through whom all things came into being.

refs.text_gb: 关于吃祭偶像之物，我们晓得偶像在世上算不得什么，也晓得神只有一位，再没有别的神。
refs.text_big5: 關於喫祭偶像之物，我們曉得偶像在世上算不得甚麼，也曉得神只有一位，再沒有別的神。
refs.text_en: Therefore concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world and that there is no God but one.

refs.text_gb: 一位众人的神与父，就是那超越众人，贯彻众人，也在众人之内的。
refs.text_big5: 一位眾人的神與父，就是那超越眾人，貫徹眾人，也在眾人之內的。
refs.text_en: One God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.

refs.text_gb: 我们岂不都有一位父么？岂不是一位神所造的么？我们各人怎么以诡诈待弟兄，渎犯了神与我们列祖所立的约呢？
refs.text_big5: 我們豈不都有一位父麼？豈不是一位神所造的麼？我們各人怎麼以詭詐待弟兄，瀆犯了神與我們列祖所立的約呢？
refs.text_en: Have we not all one Father? Has not one God created us? Why are we treacherous, each one to his brother, thus profaning the covenant of our fathers?

refs.text_gb: 因这缘故，我向父屈膝，
refs.text_big5: 因這緣故，我向父屈膝，
refs.text_en: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father,

refs.text_gb: 在诸天里以及在地上的各家族，都是从祂得名，
refs.text_big5: 在諸天裏以及在地上的各家族，都是從祂得名，
refs.text_en: Of whom every family in the heavens and on earth is named,

refs.text_gb: 因为万有都是本于祂、借着祂、并归于祂；愿荣耀归与祂，直到永远。阿们。
refs.text_big5: 因為萬有都是本於祂、藉著祂、並歸於祂；願榮耀歸與祂，直到永遠。阿們。
refs.text_en: Because out from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever. Amen.

refs.text_gb: 原来万有因祂而有，借祂而造的那位，为着要领许多的儿子进荣耀里去，就借着苦难成全他们救恩的创始者，这对祂本是合宜的。
refs.text_big5: 原來萬有因祂而有，藉祂而造的那位，為著要領許多的兒子進榮耀裏去，就藉著苦難成全他們救恩的創始者，這對祂本是合宜的。
refs.text_en: For it was fitting for Him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, in leading many sons into glory, to make the Author of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

refs.text_gb: 一主，一信，一浸；
refs.text_big5: 一主，一信，一浸；
refs.text_en: One Lord, one faith, one baptism;

refs.text_gb: 所以，以色列全家当确实地知道，你们钉在十字架上的这位耶稣，神已经立祂为主为基督了。
refs.text_big5: 所以，以色列全家當確實的知道，你們釘在十字架上的這位耶穌，神已經立祂為主為基督了。
refs.text_en: Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly that God has made Him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you have crucified.

refs.text_gb: 万口都要公开承认耶稣基督为主，使荣耀归与父神。
refs.text_big5: 萬口都要公開承認耶穌基督為主，使榮耀歸與父神。
refs.text_en: And every tongue should openly confess that Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father.

refs.text_gb: 万物是借着祂成的；凡已成的，没有一样不是借着祂成的。
refs.text_big5: 萬物是藉著祂成的；凡已成的，沒有一樣不是藉著祂成的。
refs.text_en: All things came into being through Him, and apart from Him not one thing came into being which has come into being.

refs.text_gb: 因为万有，无论是在诸天之上的、在地上的、能看见的、不能看见的、或是有位的、主治的、执政的、掌权的，都是在祂里面造的；万有都是借着祂并为着祂造的；
refs.text_big5: 因為萬有，無論是在諸天之上的、在地上的、能看見的、不能看見的、或是有位的、主治的、執政的、掌權的，都是在祂裏面造的；萬有都是藉著祂並為著祂造的；
refs.text_en: Because in Him all things were created, in the heavens and on the earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones or lordships or rulers or authorities; all things have been created through Him and unto Him.

verses.text_gb: 然而人不都有[Cra]这等知识；有人直到如今还带着拜偶像的习惯感，就以为所[Crb]吃的是祭[Crc]偶像之物；他们的[Fn1][Crd]良心既然软弱，就[Fn2]受了玷污。
verses.text_big5: 然而人不都有[Cra]這等知識；有人直到如今還帶著拜偶像的習慣感，就以為所[Crb]喫的是祭[Crc]偶像之物；他們的[Fn1][Crd]良心既然軟弱，就[Fn2]受了玷污。
verses.text_en: But this knowledge is not in all men; but some, being accustomed to the idol until now, eat the food as an idol sacrifice, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
verses.text_gb_plain: 然而人不都有这等知识；有人直到如今还带着拜偶像的习惯感，就以为所吃的是祭偶像之物；他们的良心既然软弱，就受了玷污。
verses.text_big5_plain: 然而人不都有這等知識；有人直到如今還帶著拜偶像的習慣感，就以為所喫的是祭偶像之物；他們的良心既然軟弱，就受了玷污。

footnotes.zh: 软弱的良心是由于缺少正确充足的知识。这指明我们的知识与我们的良心极其有关。有从前拜偶像，现在信基督的人，直到如今还带着拜偶像的习惯感，缺少“偶像算不得什么”(4)的知识。因此，关于偶像的事，他们的良心是软弱的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 軟弱的良心是由於缺少正確充足的知識。這指明我們的知識與我們的良心極其有關。有從前拜偶像，現在信基督的人，直到如今還帶著拜偶像的習慣感，缺少“偶像算不得甚麼”（4）的知識。因此，關於偶像的事，他們的良心是軟弱的。
footnotes.en: 8:7 1 conscience A weak conscience is due to the lack of proper and adequate knowledge. This indicates that our knowledge has much to do with our conscience. The ex-idol worshippers who are now believers in Christ, being accustomed to the idol until now, lack the knowledge that an idol is nothing (v. 4). Thus, their conscience is weak concerning the matter of idols.

footnotes.zh: 软弱的良心因对某件事缺少充足的知识，在那件事上被摸着时，就受了玷污。
footnotes.zh_big5: 軟弱的良心因對某件事缺少充足的知識，在那件事上被摸著時，就受了玷污。
footnotes.en: 8:7 2 defiled The weak conscience is defiled when it is touched by any matter about which it lacks adequate knowledge.

refs.text_gb: 关于吃祭偶像之物，我们晓得偶像在世上算不得什么，也晓得神只有一位，再没有别的神。
refs.text_big5: 關於喫祭偶像之物，我們曉得偶像在世上算不得甚麼，也曉得神只有一位，再沒有別的神。
refs.text_en: Therefore concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world and that there is no God but one.

refs.text_gb: 但那疑惑的人若吃了，就必被定罪，因为不是出于信心。凡不是出于信心的，都是罪。
refs.text_big5: 但那疑惑的人若喫了，就必被定罪，因為不是出於信心。凡不是出於信心的，都是罪。
refs.text_en: But he who doubts is condemned if he eats, because it is not out of faith; for all that is not out of faith is sin.

refs.text_gb: 关于祭偶像之物，我们晓得我们都有知识。知识是叫人自高自大，唯有爱建造人。
refs.text_big5: 關於祭偶像之物，我們曉得我們都有知識。知識是叫人自高自大，惟有愛建造人。
refs.text_en: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

refs.text_gb: 若有人见你这有知识的，在偶像的庙里坐席，这人既是软弱的，他的良心岂不放胆去吃那祭偶像之物么？
refs.text_big5: 若有人見你這有知識的，在偶像的廟裏坐席，這人既是軟弱的，他的良心豈不放膽去喫那祭偶像之物麼？
refs.text_en: For if anyone sees you who have knowledge reclining at table in an idol temple, will not his conscience, if he is weak, be emboldened to eat the things sacrificed to the idols?

refs.text_gb: 你们这样得罪弟兄们，伤了他们软弱的良心，就是得罪基督。
refs.text_big5: 你們這樣得罪弟兄們，傷了他們軟弱的良心，就是得罪基督。
refs.text_en: And sinning in this way against the brothers and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

refs.text_gb: 凡肉市上所卖的，你们只管吃，不要为良心的缘故查问什么，
refs.text_big5: 凡肉市上所賣的，你們只管喫，不要為良心的緣故查問甚麼，
refs.text_en: Everything sold in a meat market eat, asking no question for conscience' sake;

refs.text_gb: 但若有人对你们说，这是献过祭的物，就要为那指出的人，并为良心的缘故，不吃；
refs.text_big5: 但若有人對你們說，這是獻過祭的物，就要為那指出的人，並為良心的緣故，不喫；
refs.text_en: But if anyone says to you, This has been offered in sacrifice, do not eat, for his sake who pointed it out and for conscience' sake.

refs.text_gb: 我说的良心，不是你自己的，乃是别人的。我这自由为什么被别人的良心审判？
refs.text_big5: 我說的良心，不是你自己的，乃是別人的。我這自由為甚麼被別人的良心審判？
refs.text_en: Conscience, I say, not your own, but the other's. For why is my freedom judged by some other conscience?

verses.text_gb: 其实[Cra]食物不能将我们荐与神，因为我们不吃也无亏缺，吃也无[Fn1]盈超。
verses.text_big5: 其實[Cra]食物不能將我們薦與神，因為我們不喫也無虧缺，喫也無[Fn1]盈超。
verses.text_en: But food will not commend us to God; neither if we do not eat are we lacking, nor if we eat do we abound.
verses.text_gb_plain: 其实食物不能将我们荐与神，因为我们不吃也无亏缺，吃也无盈超。
verses.text_big5_plain: 其實食物不能將我們薦與神，因為我們不喫也無虧缺，喫也無盈超。

footnotes.zh: 原文意，满溢以致充盈超越——盈超。在此，指吃祭偶像之物不能叫我们在神面前，在任何方面有什么充盈和超越；所以不吃也没有什么与盈超相对的亏缺。
footnotes.zh_big5: 原文意，滿溢以致充盈超越─盈超。在此，指喫祭偶像之物不能叫我們在神面前，在任何方面有甚麼充盈和超越；所以不喫也沒有甚麼與盈超相對的虧缺。
footnotes.en: 8:8 1 abound The Greek word means to abound so that one becomes full and excelling; hence, become full and excelling. Here it denotes that eating things sacrificed to idols cannot cause us to become full and excelling in any respect before God; therefore, neither can not eating cause us to be lacking, which is in contrast to being full and excelling.

refs.text_gb: 因为神的国不在于吃喝，乃在于公义、和平、并圣灵中的喜乐。
refs.text_big5: 因為神的國不在於喫喝，乃在於公義、和平、並聖靈中的喜樂。
refs.text_en: For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.

verses.text_gb: 只是你们要谨慎，恐怕你们这[Fn1]权利，竟成了那[Fn2][Cra]软弱人的[Crb]绊脚石。
verses.text_big5: 只是你們要謹慎，恐怕你們這[Fn1]權利，竟成了那[Fn2][Cra]軟弱人的[Crb]絆腳石。
verses.text_en: But beware lest somehow this right of yours become a stumbling block to the weak ones.
verses.text_gb_plain: 只是你们要谨慎，恐怕你们这权利，竟成了那软弱人的绊脚石。
verses.text_big5_plain: 只是你們要謹慎，恐怕你們這權利，竟成了那軟弱人的絆腳石。

footnotes.zh: 或，自由。直译，权柄。与九4～5者同。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，自由。直譯，權柄。與九4～5者同。
footnotes.en: 8:9 1 right Or, liberty. Lit., authority. So also in 1 Cor. 9:4-5.

footnotes.zh: 指因缺少知识，良心软弱的人。

footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，被建造。指軟弱信徒的良心被建造起來，放膽去作已往不敢作的。這是一種突然的建造，沒有合理、堅實的根基，因此是一種不正確的建造，實際上反而毀壞人。軟弱信徒的良心放膽去喫那祭偶像之物，至終毀壞了他們，因為他們沒有充足的知識，支持他們放膽卻仍舊軟弱的良心。
footnotes.en: 8:10 1 emboldened Lit., built up. The conscience of the weak believers will be built up with boldness to do what it formerly dared not do. This is a sudden building up without a logical and solid foundation. Hence, it is an improper building up that actually ruins. Although the conscience of the weak believers is emboldened to eat what has been sacrificed to idols, such a practice will eventually ruin them because they do not have adequate knowledge to support their emboldened yet still weak conscience.

footnotes.en: 9:1 2 free The apostle Paul was free from all men, being enslaved to no one (v. 19). As all believers in Christ should be, he was free also from the bondage of any particular way of eating, although he practiced the principle of considerate love.

footnotes.zh: 使徒把自己当作信徒的榜样时，说到他的使徒职分。这使他有权柄对付本书所论到的一切难处，就是关于召会生活及其交通的严重难处。他处理这些难处，不仅基于他的教训，也基于他使徒职分所有的权柄。要对付这种光景，他必须取这立场，并使哥林多的信徒清楚这事。他们怀疑他的使徒职分，并陷于混乱的光景，主要的是由于他们因属世的智慧、自信与骄傲而有的愚昧。 “使徒，”原文意受差遣者。主的使徒，乃是受祂差遣，有祂的权柄传神的福音，教导神圣的真理，并建立众召会的信徒。在行传第一段，彼得和约翰是这样的使徒(在犹太人中间)。在行传第二段，保罗和巴拿巴是这样的使徒(在外邦人中间)。接着他们，有些人也成了使徒，如西拉和提摩太(帖前一1，二6)。只要人有能力传福音，有恩赐教导神圣的真理，并且能建立召会，他就有资格并得印证，是受主差遣、有主使命和权柄的使徒。
footnotes.zh_big5: 使徒把自己當作信徒的榜樣時，說到他的使徒職分。這使他有權柄對付本書所論到的一切難處，就是關於召會生活及其交通的嚴重難處。他處理這些難處，不僅基於他的教訓，也基於他使徒職分所有的權柄。要對付這種光景，他必須取這立場，並使哥林多的信徒清楚這事。他們懷疑他的使徒職分，並陷於混亂的光景，主要的是由於他們因屬世的智慧、自信與驕傲而有的愚昧。ˍ“使徒，”原文意受差遣者。主的使徒，乃是受祂差遣，有祂的權柄傳神的福音，教導神聖的真理，並建立眾召會的信徒。在行傳第一段，彼得和約翰是這樣的使徒（在猶太人中間）。在行傳第二段，保羅和巴拿巴是這樣的使徒（在外邦人中間）。接著他們，有些人也成了使徒，如西拉和提摩太。（帖前一1，二6。）只要人有能力傳福音，有恩賜教導神聖的真理，並且能建立召會，他就有資格並得印證，是受主差遣、有主使命和權柄的使徒。
footnotes.en: 9:1 3 apostle As he presented himself a pattern to the believers, the apostle came to the matter of his apostleship, which gave him authority to deal with all the problems covered in this book, serious problems concerning the church life and its fellowship. His handling of these problems was based not only on his teaching but also on the authority inherent in his apostleship. To deal with the situation, he had to take this standing and make this matter clear to the Corinthian believers. They had questioned his apostleship and were in a chaotic situation, mainly because of the foolishness of their worldly wisdom, self-confidence, and pride. The Greek word for apostle means one who is sent. An apostle of the Lord is a believer who is sent out by Him with His authority to preach the gospel of God, to teach the divine truth, and to establish churches. In the first section of Acts, Peter and John were such apostles among the Jews, and in the second section of Acts, Paul and Barnabas were such apostles among the Gentiles. After them, others also became apostles, such as Silas (i.e., Silvanus) and Timothy (1 Thes. 1:1; 2:6). As long as one has the power to preach the gospel, the gift to teach the divine truth, and the ability to establish churches, he is qualified and confirmed to be an apostle sent by the Lord with His commission and authority.

footnotes.zh: 指保罗见过主荣耀、复活的身体(十五5～8)。这是格外的特权，对看见者构成尊贵与荣耀，但不是作主使徒的条件或资格。这由巴拿巴的例子，充分得着证明。巴拿巴是使徒之一(徒十四14)，却没有这样见过主。然而，在灵里借属灵的启示认识主，确是作使徒所需要的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 指保羅見過主榮耀、復活的身體。（十五5～8。）這是格外的特權，對看見者構成尊貴與榮耀，但不是作主使徒的條件或資格。這由巴拿巴的例子，充分得著證明。巴拿巴是使徒之一，（徒十四14，）卻沒有這樣見過主。然而，在靈裏藉屬靈的啟示認識主，確是作使徒所需要的。
footnotes.en: 9:1 4 seen This refers to Paul's having seen the Lord in His glorious resurrected body (1 Cor. 15:5-8). This is a special privilege; it constitutes some dignity and glory to the seer, but it is not a requirement or qualification for being the Lord's apostle. This is fully proven by the case of Barnabas, who was one of the apostles (Acts 14:14) yet did not see the Lord in this way. However, to know the Lord in spirit by spiritual revelation is definitely needed for one to be an apostle.

footnotes.zh: 保罗在主里的工作有果效，是他使徒职分的证明，而不是资格。
footnotes.zh_big5: 保羅在主裏的工作有果效，是他使徒職分的證明，而不是資格。
footnotes.en: 9:1 5 work The fruitful result of his work in the Lord was a proof of, not a qualification for, Paul's apostleship.

verses.text_gb: 独有我与[Cra]巴拿巴没有[Crb]权利不作工么？
verses.text_big5: 獨有我與[Cra]巴拿巴沒有[Crb]權利不作工麼？
verses.text_en: Or do only I and Barnabas not have the right not to work?
verses.text_gb_plain: 独有我与巴拿巴没有权利不作工么？
verses.text_big5_plain: 獨有我與巴拿巴沒有權利不作工麼？

refs.text_gb: 他们事奉主，禁食的时候，圣灵说，要为我分别巴拿巴和扫罗，去作我召他们所作的工。
refs.text_big5: 他們事奉主，禁食的時候，聖靈說，要為我分別巴拿巴和掃羅，去作我召他們所作的工。
refs.text_en: And as they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, Set apart for Me now Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.

refs.text_gb: 过了十四年，我同巴拿巴，也带着提多，再上耶路撒冷去。
refs.text_big5: 過了十四年，我同巴拿巴，也帶著提多，再上耶路撒冷去。
refs.text_en: Then after a period of fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus with me also.

refs.text_gb: 又知道所赐给我的恩典，那被视为柱石的雅各、矶法、约翰，就向我和巴拿巴伸出右手彼此相交，叫我们往外邦人那里去，他们却往受割礼的人那里去；
refs.text_big5: 又知道所賜給我的恩典，那被視為柱石的雅各、磯法、約翰，就向我和巴拿巴伸出右手彼此相交，叫我們往外邦人那裏去，他們卻往受割禮的人那裏去；
refs.text_en: And perceiving the grace given to me, James and Cephas and John, who were reputed to be pillars, gave to me and to Barnabas the right hand of fellowship that we should go to the Gentiles, and they, to the circumcision.

refs.text_gb: 这并不是因我们没有权利，乃是要给你们作榜样，叫你们效法我们。
refs.text_big5: 這並不是因我們沒有權利，乃是要給你們作榜樣，叫你們效法我們。
refs.text_en: Not because we do not have the right, but in order that we might give ourselves to you as a pattern that you might imitate us.

verses.text_gb: 有谁[Cra]当兵，曾自备粮饷？有谁[Crb]栽种[Crc]葡萄园，不[Crd]吃园中的果子？有谁牧养羊群，不吃羊群的奶？
verses.text_big5: 有誰[Cra]當兵，曾自備糧餉？有誰[Crb]栽種[Crc]葡萄園，不[Crd]喫園中的果子？有誰牧養羊群，不喫羊群的奶？
verses.text_en: What soldier ever serves by his own wages? Who plants a vineyard and does not partake of its fruit? Or who shepherds a flock and does not partake of the milk of the flock?
verses.text_gb_plain: 有谁当兵，曾自备粮饷？有谁栽种葡萄园，不吃园中的果子？有谁牧养羊群，不吃羊群的奶？
verses.text_big5_plain: 有誰當兵，曾自備糧餉？有誰栽種葡萄園，不喫園中的果子？有誰牧養羊群，不喫羊群的奶？

refs.text_gb: 孩子提摩太，我照从前指着你所说的预言，将这嘱咐交托你，叫你凭这些预言，可以打那美好的仗，
refs.text_big5: 孩子提摩太，我照從前指著你所說的豫言，將這囑咐交託你，叫你憑這些豫言，可以打那美好的仗，
refs.text_en: This charge I commit to you, my child Timothy, according to the prophecies previously made concerning you, that by them you might war the good warfare,

refs.text_gb: 你要和我同受苦难，好像基督耶稣的精兵。
refs.text_big5: 你要和我同受苦難，好像基督耶穌的精兵。
refs.text_en: Suffer evil with me as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

refs.text_gb: 凡当兵的，不让今生的事务缠身，好叫那招他入伍的人喜悦。
refs.text_big5: 凡當兵的，不讓今生的事務纏身，好叫那招他入伍的人喜悅。
refs.text_en: No one serving as a soldier entangles himself with the affairs of this life, that he may please the one who enlisted him.

refs.text_gb: 我栽种了，亚波罗浇灌了，唯有神叫他生长。
refs.text_big5: 我栽種了，亞波羅澆灌了，惟有神叫他生長。
refs.text_en: I planted, Apollos watered, but God caused the growth.

refs.text_gb: 可见栽种的算不得什么，浇灌的也算不得什么，只在那叫他生长的神。
refs.text_big5: 可見栽種的算不得甚麼，澆灌的也算不得甚麼，只在那叫他生長的神。
refs.text_en: So then neither is he who plants anything nor he who waters, but God who causes the growth.

refs.text_gb: 栽种的和浇灌的都是一样，但将来各人要照自己的劳苦，得自己的赏赐。
refs.text_big5: 栽種的和澆灌的都是一樣，但將來各人要照自己的勞苦，得自己的賞賜。
refs.text_en: Now he who plants and he who waters are one, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.

refs.text_gb: 有谁种葡萄园，尚未享用呢？他可以回家去，免得他阵亡，别人去享用。
refs.text_big5: 有誰種葡萄園，尚未享用呢？他可以回家去，免得他陣亡，別人去享用。
refs.text_en: Is there any man who has planted a vineyard and has not partaken of it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man partake of it.

refs.text_gb: 所罗门在巴力哈们有一葡萄园：他将这葡萄园交给看守的人，每人要为其中的果子交一千舍客勒银子。
refs.text_big5: 所羅門在巴力哈們有一葡萄園：他將這葡萄園交給看守的人，每人要為其中的果子交一千舍客勒銀子。
refs.text_en: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon: / He let out the vineyard to keepers; / Each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.

refs.text_gb: 我自己的葡萄园在我面前。所罗门哪，一千舍客勒归你，二百舍客勒归看守果子的人。
refs.text_big5: 我自己的葡萄園在我面前。所羅門哪，一千舍客勒歸你，二百舍客勒歸看守果子的人。
refs.text_en: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me. / You will have the thousand, O Solomon; / And those who keep its fruit, two hundred.

refs.text_gb: 看守无花果树的，必吃树上的果子；看护主人的，必得尊荣。
refs.text_big5: 看守無花果樹的，必喫樹上的果子；看護主人的，必得尊榮。
refs.text_en: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, / And he who takes care of his master will be honored.

refs.text_gb: 你们岂不知为圣事劳碌的，就吃殿中之物么？伺候祭坛的，就同祭坛分领坛上的祭物么？
refs.text_big5: 你們豈不知為聖事勞碌的，就喫殿中之物麼？伺候祭壇的，就同祭壇分領壇上的祭物麼？
refs.text_en: Do you not know that those who labor on the sacred things eat the things of the sacred temple, that those who attend to the altar have their portion with the altar?

verses.text_gb: 我说这话，岂是[Cra]照着人的看法么？律法不也是这样说么？
verses.text_big5: 我說這話，豈是[Cra]照著人的看法麼？律法不也是這樣說麼？
verses.text_en: Am I speaking these things according to man? Or does the law not also say these things?
verses.text_gb_plain: 我说这话，岂是照着人的看法么？律法不也是这样说么？
verses.text_big5_plain: 我說這話，豈是照著人的看法麼？律法不也是這樣說麼？

refs.text_gb: 我且照着人的常话说，我们的不义若显出神的义来，我们要说什么？神降怒，难道是祂不义么？
refs.text_big5: 我且照著人的常話說，我們的不義若顯出神的義來，我們要說甚麼？神降怒，難道是祂不義麼？
refs.text_en: But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is the God who inflicts wrath unrighteous? I speak according to man.

verses.text_gb: 在摩西的律法上记着：“[Fn1][Cra]牛踹谷的时候，不可笼住它的嘴。”难道神所关心的是牛么？
verses.text_big5: 在摩西的律法上記著：“[Fn1][Cra]牛踹穀的時候，不可籠住牠的嘴。”難道神所關心的是牛麼？
verses.text_en: For in the law of Moses it is written: "You shall not muzzle the ox while it is treading out the grain." Is it for oxen that God cares?
verses.text_gb_plain: 在摩西的律法上记着：“牛踹谷的时候，不可笼住它的嘴。”难道神所关心的是牛么？
verses.text_big5_plain: 在摩西的律法上記著：“牛踹穀的時候，不可籠住牠的嘴。”難道神所關心的是牛麼？

footnotes.zh: 或，不可笼住踹谷之牛的嘴。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，不可籠住踹穀之牛的嘴。
footnotes.en: 9:9 1 while Or, that is treading out the grain.

refs.text_gb: 牛踹谷的时候，不可笼住它的嘴。
refs.text_big5: 牛踹穀的時候，不可籠住牠的嘴。
refs.text_en: You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out grain.

refs.text_gb: 因为经上说，“牛踹谷的时候，不可笼住它的嘴。”又说，“作工的配得工价。”
refs.text_big5: 因為經上說，“牛踹穀的時候，不可籠住牠的嘴。”又說，“作工的配得工價。”
refs.text_en: For the Scripture says, "You shall not muzzle an ox that is treading out the grain," and, "The workman is worthy of his pay."

verses.text_gb: 还是全为我们说的？的确是为我们写的，因为[Cra]耕种的当存着指望去耕种，打场的也当存着分享的指望去打场。
verses.text_big5: 還是全為我們說的？的確是為我們寫的，因為[Cra]耕種的當存著指望去耕種，打場的也當存著分享的指望去打場。
verses.text_en: Or does He say it altogether for our sake? Yes, for our sake it was written because the plowman should plow in hope, and he who threshes, in hope of partaking.
verses.text_gb_plain: 还是全为我们说的？的确是为我们写的，因为耕种的当存着指望去耕种，打场的也当存着分享的指望去打场。
verses.text_big5_plain: 還是全為我們說的？的確是為我們寫的，因為耕種的當存著指望去耕種，打場的也當存著分享的指望去打場。

refs.text_gb: 劳力的农夫，理当先分享果实。
refs.text_big5: 勞力的農夫，理當先分享果實。
refs.text_en: The laboring farmer must be the first to partake of the fruit.

verses.text_gb: 我们若把[Cra]属灵之物撒给你们，就是从你们收割肉身之物，这还算大事么？
verses.text_big5: 我們若把[Cra]屬靈之物撒給你們，就是從你們收割肉身之物，這還算大事麼？
verses.text_en: If we have sown to you the spiritual things, is it a great thing if we shall reap from you the fleshly things?
verses.text_gb_plain: 我们若把属灵之物撒给你们，就是从你们收割肉身之物，这还算大事么？
verses.text_big5_plain: 我們若把屬靈之物撒給你們，就是從你們收割肉身之物，這還算大事麼？

refs.text_gb: 这是他们乐意的，其实也是他们所欠的债。因外邦人既然分享犹太人属灵的事物，就当供给他们肉身之物。
refs.text_big5: 這是他們樂意的，其實也是他們所欠的債。因外邦人既然分享猶太人屬靈的事物，就當供給他們肉身之物。
refs.text_en: For they were pleased to do it, and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual things, they ought also to do service to them in material things.

verses.text_gb: 若别人在你们身上分享这权利，何况我们？然而我们[Cra]没有用过这权利，倒凡事[Fn1]忍受，[Crb]免得基督的福音受到任何拦阻。
verses.text_big5: 若別人在你們身上分享這權利，何況我們？然而我們[Cra]沒有用過這權利，倒凡事[Fn1]忍受，[Crb]免得基督的福音受到任何攔阻。
verses.text_en: If others partake of this right over you, should not rather we? Yet we did not use this right, but we bear all things that we may not cause any hindrance to the gospel of Christ.
verses.text_gb_plain: 若别人在你们身上分享这权利，何况我们？然而我们没有用过这权利，倒凡事忍受，免得基督的福音受到任何拦阻。
verses.text_big5_plain: 若別人在你們身上分享這權利，何況我們？然而我們沒有用過這權利，倒凡事忍受，免得基督的福音受到任何攔阻。

footnotes.zh: 或，容忍。直译，(如器皿)容纳，隐藏。因此是指(如屋顶)遮盖。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，容忍。直譯，（如器皿）容納，隱藏。因此是指（如屋頂）遮蓋。
footnotes.en: 9:12 1 bear Or, endure. Lit., contain (as a vessel), conceal; hence, cover (as a roof ).

refs.text_gb: 但这些权利我全没有用过；我写这些话，并非要你们这样待我，因为我宁可死，也不─没有人能使我所夸的落了空。
refs.text_big5: 但這些權利我全沒有用過；我寫這些話，並非要你們這樣待我，因為我寧可死，也不─沒有人能使我所誇的落了空。
refs.text_en: But I myself have not used any of these things; and I have not written these things that it may be so with me; for it is good for me rather to die than-No one shall make my boast void.

refs.text_gb: 这样，我的赏赐是什么？就是在传福音上，我免费供应福音，免得用尽我在福音上的权利。
refs.text_big5: 這樣，我的賞賜是甚麼？就是在傳福音上，我免費供應福音，免得用盡我在福音上的權利。
refs.text_en: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may present the gospel without charge, so as not to use to the full my right in the gospel.

refs.text_gb: 我在你们那里缺乏的时候，并没有累着你们一个人，因我所缺乏的，那从马其顿来的弟兄们都补足了。我向来凡事自守，不累着你们，将来也必自守。
refs.text_big5: 我在你們那裏缺乏的時候，並沒有累著你們一個人，因我所缺乏的，那從馬其頓來的弟兄們都補足了。我向來凡事自守，不累著你們，將來也必自守。
refs.text_en: And when I was present with you and lacked, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia filled up my lack, and in everything I kept myself from being burdensome to you, and will keep myself.

refs.text_gb: 这样，我的赏赐是什么？就是在传福音上，我免费供应福音，免得用尽我在福音上的权利。
refs.text_big5: 這樣，我的賞賜是甚麼？就是在傳福音上，我免費供應福音，免得用盡我在福音上的權利。
refs.text_en: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may present the gospel without charge, so as not to use to the full my right in the gospel.

refs.text_gb: 我们凡事都不使人绊跌，免得这职事被人挑剔，
refs.text_big5: 我們凡事都不使人絆跌，免得這職事被人挑剔，
refs.text_en: We give no occasion of stumbling in anything that the ministry may not be faulted,

refs.text_gb: 弟兄们，你们原记得我们的劳碌辛苦；我们是昼夜作工，把神的福音传扬给你们，免得叫你们任何人受累。
refs.text_big5: 弟兄們，你們原記得我們的勞碌辛苦；我們是晝夜作工，把神的福音傳揚給你們，免得叫你們任何人受累。
refs.text_en: For you remember, brothers, our labor and travail: While working night and day so as not to be burdensome to any of you, we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.

refs.text_gb: 也未尝白吃任何人的饭，倒是劳碌辛苦，昼夜作工，免得叫你们任何人受累。
refs.text_big5: 也未嘗白喫任何人的飯，倒是勞碌辛苦，晝夜作工，免得叫你們任何人受累。
refs.text_en: Nor did we eat bread as a gift from anyone, but in labor and hardship we worked night and day so that we would not be burdensome to any of you;

verses.text_gb: 你们岂不知为[Fn1]圣事劳碌的，就[Cra]吃殿中之物么？伺候祭坛的，就同祭坛分领坛上的祭物么？
verses.text_big5: 你們豈不知為[Fn1]聖事勞碌的，就[Cra]喫殿中之物麼？伺候祭壇的，就同祭壇分領壇上的祭物麼？
verses.text_en: Do you not know that those who labor on the sacred things eat the things of the sacred temple, that those who attend to the altar have their portion with the altar?

verses.text_big5_plain: 你們豈不知為聖事勞碌的，就喫殿中之物麼？伺候祭壇的，就同祭壇分領壇上的祭物麼？

footnotes.zh: 圣，与罗一2者和路一75者都不同，与提后三15者同；指在关于敬拜神之事上的圣。
footnotes.zh_big5: 聖，與羅一2者和路一75者都不同，與提後三15者同；指在關於敬拜神之事上的聖。
footnotes.en: 9:13 1 sacred The word for sacred here is different from the word for holy in Rom. 1:2 and the word for holiness in Luke 1:75, and is the same as the word for sacred in 2 Tim. 3:15. It denotes the sacredness of the things that are related to the worship of God.

refs.text_gb: 所剩下的，亚伦和他子孙要吃，必在圣处不带酵而吃，要在会幕的院子里吃。
refs.text_big5: 所剩下的，亞倫和他子孫要喫，必在聖處不帶酵而喫，要在會幕的院子裏喫。
refs.text_en: And what is left of it Aaron and his sons may eat; it shall be eaten without leaven in a holy place; in the court of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it.

refs.text_gb: 为罪献这祭的祭司要吃这祭物，要在圣处，就是在会幕的院子里吃。
refs.text_big5: 為罪獻這祭的祭司要喫這祭物，要在聖處，就是在會幕的院子裏喫。
refs.text_en: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. In a holy place it shall be eaten, in the court of the Tent of Meeting.

refs.text_gb: 耶和华对亚伦说，我已将我的举祭，就是以色列人一切分别为圣的物，交给你经管；因你受过膏，我把这些都赐给了你和你的子孙；这要作永远的定例。
refs.text_big5: 耶和華對亞倫說，我已將我的舉祭，就是以色列人一切分別為聖的物，交給你經管；因你受過膏，我把這些都賜給了你和你的子孫；這要作永遠的定例。
refs.text_en: Then Jehovah spoke to Aaron, And I Myself have given you charge of My heave offerings, even all the holy things of the children of Israel; I have given them to you because of the anointing, and to your sons, as a perpetual statute.

refs.text_gb: 至圣之物中不经过火的，都是你的；以色列人给我的一切供物，就是一切的素祭、赎罪祭、赎愆祭，都是至圣的，要归给你和你的子孙。
refs.text_big5: 至聖之物中不經過火的，都是你的；以色列人給我的一切供物，就是一切的素祭、贖罪祭、贖愆祭，都是至聖的，要歸給你和你的子孫。
refs.text_en: This shall be yours of the most holy things, kept from the fire. Every offering of theirs, even every meal offering of theirs and every sin offering of theirs and every trespass offering of theirs, which they shall render to Me, shall be most holy for you and for your sons.

refs.text_gb: 你要拿这些当至圣物吃；凡男丁都可以吃；你当以此物为圣。
refs.text_big5: 你要拿這些當至聖物喫；凡男丁都可以喫；你當以此物為聖。
refs.text_en: As the most holy things you shall eat it; every male shall eat it; it shall be holy to you.

refs.text_gb: 以色列人礼物中的举祭，并一切的摇祭，也都是你的，我已赐给你和你的儿子并女儿；这要作永远的定例；凡在你家中洁净的人都可以吃。
refs.text_big5: 以色列人禮物中的舉祭，並一切的搖祭，也都是你的，我已賜給你和你的兒子並女兒；這要作永遠的定例；凡在你家中潔淨的人都可以喫。
refs.text_en: This also is yours, the heave offering of their gift, even all the wave offerings of the children of Israel. I have given them to you and to your sons and to your daughters with you, as a perpetual statute; everyone who is clean in your house may eat it.

refs.text_gb: 凡油中至好的，凡新酒和五谷中至好的，就是以色列人所献给耶和华的初熟之物，我都赐给你。
refs.text_big5: 凡油中至好的，凡新酒和五穀中至好的，就是以色列人所獻給耶和華的初熟之物，我都賜給你。
refs.text_en: All the best of the oil, and all the best of the new wine and of the grain, their firstfruits that they give to Jehovah, I have given to you.

refs.text_gb: 凡从他们地上所带来给耶和华的初熟之物，也都要归与你；凡在你家中洁净的人都可以吃。
refs.text_big5: 凡從他們地上所帶來給耶和華的初熟之物，也都要歸與你；凡在你家中潔淨的人都可以喫。
refs.text_en: The firstfruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to Jehovah, shall be yours; everyone who is clean in your house may eat it.

refs.text_gb: 以色列中一切永献的都必归与你。
refs.text_big5: 以色列中一切永獻的都必歸與你。
refs.text_en: Everything devoted in Israel shall be yours.

refs.text_gb: 他们所奉给耶和华的，连人带牲畜，一切血肉所生，凡头胎的，都要归给你；只是人中头生的，总要赎出来；不洁净牲畜头生的，也要赎出来。
refs.text_big5: 他們所奉給耶和華的，連人帶牲畜，一切血肉所生，凡頭胎的，都要歸給你；只是人中頭生的，總要贖出來；不潔淨牲畜頭生的，也要贖出來。
refs.text_en: Everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present to Jehovah, whether human or animal, shall be yours; nevertheless the firstborn of human beings you shall surely redeem, and the firstborn of unclean animals you shall redeem.

refs.text_gb: 其中从一个月以上所当赎的，要照你所估定的价，按圣所的舍客勒，（一舍客勒是二十季拉，）用银子五舍客勒赎出来。
refs.text_big5: 其中從一個月以上所當贖的，要照你所估定的價，按聖所的舍客勒，（一舍客勒是二十季拉，）用銀子五舍客勒贖出來。
refs.text_en: And those who are to be redeemed from a month old you shall redeem, according to your estimation, for five shekels of silver, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs.

refs.text_gb: 只是头生的牛、头生的绵羊、或头生的山羊，必不可赎；它们都是圣的。你要把它们的血洒在坛上，把它们的脂油焚烧，当作怡爽香气的火祭献给耶和华。
refs.text_big5: 只是頭生的牛、頭生的綿羊、或頭生的山羊，必不可贖；牠們都是聖的。你要把牠們的血灑在壇上，把牠們的脂油焚燒，當作怡爽香氣的火祭獻給耶和華。
refs.text_en: But the firstborn of a cow or the firstborn of a sheep or the firstborn of a goat you shall not redeem; they are holy. You shall sprinkle their blood upon the altar and burn their fat as an offering by fire for a satisfying fragrance to Jehovah.

refs.text_gb: 它们的肉必归与你，像摇祭的胸、举祭的右腿归与你一样。
refs.text_big5: 牠們的肉必歸與你，像搖祭的胸、舉祭的右腿歸與你一樣。
refs.text_en: But their flesh shall be yours; like the breast of the wave offering and like the right thigh, it shall be yours.

refs.text_gb: 凡以色列人所献给耶和华圣物中的举祭，我都赐给你和你的儿子并女儿；这要作永远的定例。这是给你和你的后裔，在耶和华面前作为永远的盐约。
refs.text_big5: 凡以色列人所獻給耶和華聖物中的舉祭，我都賜給你和你的兒子並女兒；這要作永遠的定例。這是給你和你的後裔，在耶和華面前作為永遠的鹽約。
refs.text_en: All the heave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer to Jehovah, I have given to you and to your sons and your daughters with you, as a perpetual statute. It is a covenant of salt forever before Jehovah for you and for your descendants with you.

refs.text_gb: 耶和华对亚伦说，你在以色列人的地上不可有产业，在他们中间也不可有分；在他们中间，我就是你的分，是你的产业。
refs.text_big5: 耶和華對亞倫說，你在以色列人的地上不可有產業，在他們中間也不可有分；在他們中間，我就是你的分，是你的產業。
refs.text_en: And Jehovah said to Aaron, You shall have no inheritance in their land, nor shall you have any portion among them; I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Israel.

refs.text_gb: 你们和你们的家属随处可以吃，因为这是你们的赏赐，作你们在会幕里办事的报酬。
refs.text_big5: 你們和你們的家屬隨處可以喫，因為這是你們的賞賜，作你們在會幕裏辦事的報酬。
refs.text_en: And you may eat it in every place, you and your households, for it is your reward in return for your service in the Tent of Meeting.

refs.text_gb: 祭司利未人和利未全支派，必在以色列中无分无业；他们要吃用献给耶和华的火祭和祂的产业。
refs.text_big5: 祭司利未人和利未全支派，必在以色列中無分無業；他們要喫用獻給耶和華的火祭和祂的產業。
refs.text_en: The Levitical priests and the whole tribe of Levi shall have no portion or inheritance with Israel; they shall eat Jehovah's offerings by fire and His inheritance.

verses.text_gb: 主也是这样命定，叫宣传福音的[Cra]靠福音养生。
verses.text_big5: 主也是這樣命定，叫宣傳福音的[Cra]靠福音養生。
verses.text_en: So also the Lord directed those who announce the gospel to live from the gospel.
verses.text_gb_plain: 主也是这样命定，叫宣传福音的靠福音养生。
verses.text_big5_plain: 主也是這樣命定，叫宣傳福音的靠福音養生。

refs.text_gb: 难道我们没有权利吃喝么？
refs.text_big5: 難道我們沒有權利喫喝麼？
refs.text_en: Do we not have a right to eat and to drink?

refs.text_gb: 行路不要带口袋，不要带两件里衣，也不要带鞋和手杖，因为作工的配得食物。
refs.text_big5: 行路不要帶口袋，不要帶兩件裏衣，也不要帶鞋和手杖，因為作工的配得食物。
refs.text_en: No bag for the journey nor two tunics nor sandals nor a staff; for the worker is worthy of his food.

refs.text_gb: 你们要住在那家，吃喝他们所供给的，因为作工的配得工价。不要从这家搬到那家。
refs.text_big5: 你們要住在那家，喫喝他們所供給的，因為作工的配得工價。不要從這家搬到那家。
refs.text_en: And in that house remain, eating and drinking the things from them, for the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move from house to house.

refs.text_gb: 无论进哪一城，人若接待你们，给你们摆上什么，你们就吃什么。
refs.text_big5: 無論進那一城，人若接待你們，給你們擺上甚麼，你們就喫甚麼。
refs.text_en: And into whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you;

verses.text_gb: 但这些权利我全[Cra]没有用过；我写这些话，并非要你们这样待我，因为我[Fn1]宁可死，也[Fn2]不─没有人能使我所[Crb]夸的落了空。
verses.text_big5: 但這些權利我全[Cra]沒有用過；我寫這些話，並非要你們這樣待我，因為我[Fn1]寧可死，也[Fn2]不─沒有人能使我所[Crb]誇的落了空。
verses.text_en: But I myself have not used any of these things; and I have not written these things that it may be so with me; for it is good for me rather to die than-No one shall make my boast void.
verses.text_gb_plain: 但这些权利我全没有用过；我写这些话，并非要你们这样待我，因为我宁可死，也不─没有人能使我所夸的落了空。
verses.text_big5_plain: 但這些權利我全沒有用過；我寫這些話，並非要你們這樣待我，因為我寧可死，也不─沒有人能使我所誇的落了空。

footnotes.zh: 使徒乃是不顾一切，绝对为着主的权益。他不仅甘愿牺牲一切的权利(12，15上，18)，甚至甘愿付出性命的代价。
footnotes.zh_big5: 使徒乃是不顧一切，絕對為著主的權益。他不僅甘願犧牲一切的權利，（12，15上，18，）甚至甘願付出性命的代價。
footnotes.en: 9:15 1 rather The apostle was desperately absolute for the Lord's interests. He was willing not only to sacrifice all his rights (vv. 12, 15, 18) but also to pay the price even of his life.

footnotes.zh: 也不什么，保罗未说下去。可能是前半节所提之事。
footnotes.zh_big5: 也不甚麼，保羅未說下去。可能是前半節所題之事。
footnotes.en: 9:15 2 than Than what? Paul did not finish the sentence. Perhaps he was referring to the things mentioned in the first half of this verse.

refs.text_gb: 若别人在你们身上分享这权利，何况我们？然而我们没有用过这权利，倒凡事忍受，免得基督的福音受到任何拦阻。
refs.text_big5: 若別人在你們身上分享這權利，何況我們？然而我們沒有用過這權利，倒凡事忍受，免得基督的福音受到任何攔阻。
refs.text_en: If others partake of this right over you, should not rather we? Yet we did not use this right, but we bear all things that we may not cause any hindrance to the gospel of Christ.

refs.text_gb: 基督的真实在我里面，这夸口在亚该亚一带，是不会在我身上被堵住的。
refs.text_big5: 基督的真實在我裏面，這誇口在亞該亞一帶，是不會在我身上被堵住的。
refs.text_en: The truthfulness of Christ is in me, that this boasting shall not be stopped as it regards me in the regions of Achaia.

verses.text_gb: 我若传福音，于我原没有可夸的，因为[Fn1][Cra]我是不得已的。若不传福音，我便有祸了。
verses.text_big5: 我若傳福音，於我原沒有可誇的，因為[Fn1][Cra]我是不得已的。若不傳福音，我便有禍了。
verses.text_en: For if I preach the gospel, I have no boast, for necessity is laid upon me; for woe to me if I do not preach the gospel.
verses.text_gb_plain: 我若传福音，于我原没有可夸的，因为我是不得已的。若不传福音，我便有祸了。
verses.text_big5_plain: 我若傳福音，於我原沒有可誇的，因為我是不得已的。若不傳福音，我便有禍了。

footnotes.zh: 直译，有难免的负担压在我身上。
footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，有難免的負擔壓在我身上。

refs.text_gb: 我若说，我不再提说祂，也不再奉祂的名讲论，我便心里觉得似乎有烧着的火，闭塞在我骨中，我就含忍不住，不能自禁。
refs.text_big5: 我若說，我不再題說祂，也不再奉祂的名講論，我便心裏覺得似乎有燒著的火，閉塞在我骨中，我就含忍不住，不能自禁。
refs.text_en: But if I say, I will not mention Him / Or speak anymore in His name, / Then it is in my heart like a burning fire, / Shut up in my bones, / And I am weary of holding it in, / Nor can I.

refs.text_gb: 因为我们所看见所听见的，不能不说。
refs.text_big5: 因為我們所看見所聽見的，不能不說。
refs.text_en: For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.

verses.text_gb: 我若甘心作这事，就有[Fn1][Cra]赏赐；若不甘心，[Fn2][Crb]管家的职分却已经[Crc]托付我了。
verses.text_big5: 我若甘心作這事，就有[Fn1][Cra]賞賜；若不甘心，[Fn2][Crb]管家的職分卻已經[Crc]託付我了。
verses.text_en: If I do this of my own will, I have a reward; but if not of my own will, I am entrusted with a stewardship.
verses.text_gb_plain: 我若甘心作这事，就有赏赐；若不甘心，管家的职分却已经托付我了。
verses.text_big5_plain: 我若甘心作這事，就有賞賜；若不甘心，管家的職分卻已經託付我了。

footnotes.zh: 使徒写本书不是为着帮助失丧的罪人得救，乃是为着帮助得救的信徒长大(三6～7)，用贵重的材料建造(三10，12～14)，顾到主的肢体(八9～13)并赛跑(24)。因此，他一再说到赏赐，作为信徒前进的激励(三14，九18，24～25)。见来十35注1。
footnotes.zh_big5: 使徒寫本書不是為著幫助失喪的罪人得救，乃是為著幫助得救的信徒長大，（三6～7，）用貴重的材料建造，（三10，12～14，）顧到主的肢體（八9～13）並賽跑。（24。）因此，他一再說到賞賜，作為信徒前進的激勵。（三14，九18，24～25。）見來十35註1。
footnotes.en: 9:17 1 reward This book was written not to help lost sinners to be saved but to help saved believers to grow (1 Cor. 3:6-7), to build with the precious materials (1 Cor. 3:10, 12-14), to care for the Lord's members (1 Cor. 8:9-13), and to run the race (v. 24). Hence, a reward is mentioned repeatedly as an incentive to the believers for their progress (1 Cor. 3:14; 9:18, 24-25). See note Heb. 10:35 1 .

footnotes.zh: 或，家庭管理，家庭分配。使徒不仅是传道者，还是神家中的管家，管理家庭的人，将基督的救恩、生命和丰富分配给祂的信徒。这样的职事，就是托付并委派他的管家职分(弗三2，林后四1)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，家庭管理，家庭分配。使徒不僅是傳道者，還是神家中的管家，管理家庭的人，將基督的救恩、生命和豐富分配給祂的信徒。這樣的職事，就是託付並委派他的管家職分。（弗三2，林後四1。）
footnotes.en: 9:17 2 stewardship Or, household administration, household dispensation. The apostle was not only a preacher but also a steward in God's house, a household administrator, dispensing Christ's salvation, life, and riches to His believers. Such a ministry was the stewardship with which he had been entrusted and commissioned (Eph. 3:2; 2 Cor. 4:1).

refs.text_gb: 栽种的和浇灌的都是一样，但将来各人要照自己的劳苦，得自己的赏赐。
refs.text_big5: 栽種的和澆灌的都是一樣，但將來各人要照自己的勞苦，得自己的賞賜。
refs.text_en: Now he who plants and he who waters are one, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.

refs.text_gb: 人在那根基上所建造的工程若存得住，他就要得赏赐。
refs.text_big5: 人在那根基上所建造的工程若存得住，他就要得賞賜。
refs.text_en: If anyone's work which he has built upon the foundation remains, he will receive a reward;

refs.text_gb: 谅必你们曾听见那为着你们所赐给我，神恩典的管家职分，
refs.text_big5: 諒必你們曾聽見那為著你們所賜給我，神恩典的管家職分，
refs.text_en: If indeed you have heard of the stewardship of the grace of God which was given to me for you,

refs.text_gb: 我照神为你们所赐我的管家职分，作了召会的执事，要完成神的话，
refs.text_big5: 我照神為你們所賜我的管家職分，作了召會的執事，要完成神的話，
refs.text_en: Of which I became a minister according to the stewardship of God, which was given to me for you, to complete the word of God,

refs.text_gb: 反倒看见我受托传福音给那未受割礼的人，正如彼得受托传福音给那受割礼的人，
refs.text_big5: 反倒看見我受託傳福音給那未受割禮的人，正如彼得受託傳福音給那受割禮的人，
refs.text_en: But on the contrary, seeing that I had been entrusted with the gospel to the uncircumcision, even as Peter with the gospel to the circumcision,

verses.text_gb: 这样，我的赏赐是什么？就是在传福音上，我[Cra]免费[Fn1]供应福音，[Crb]免得用尽我在福音上的权利。
verses.text_big5: 這樣，我的賞賜是甚麼？就是在傳福音上，我[Cra]免費[Fn1]供應福音，[Crb]免得用盡我在福音上的權利。
verses.text_en: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may present the gospel without charge, so as not to use to the full my right in the gospel.
verses.text_gb_plain: 这样，我的赏赐是什么？就是在传福音上，我免费供应福音，免得用尽我在福音上的权利。
verses.text_big5_plain: 這樣，我的賞賜是甚麼？就是在傳福音上，我免費供應福音，免得用盡我在福音上的權利。

footnotes.zh: 直译，供陈。
footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，供陳。

refs.text_gb: 我因为白白传神的福音给你们，就卑屈自己，为叫你们升高，这是我犯了罪么？
refs.text_big5: 我因為白白傳神的福音給你們，就卑屈自己，為叫你們升高，這是我犯了罪麼？
refs.text_en: Or did I commit a sin, abasing myself that you might be exalted, because I announced the gospel of God to you free of charge?

refs.text_gb: 因为除了我自己不累着你们以外，你们还有什么事不及其余的召会？这不公之处，你们饶恕我吧！
refs.text_big5: 因為除了我自己不累著你們以外，你們還有甚麼事不及其餘的召會？這不公之處，你們饒恕我罷！
refs.text_en: For what is there in which you were treated in a manner inferior to the rest of the churches, except that I myself was not a burden to you? Graciously forgive me this injustice!

refs.text_gb: 若别人在你们身上分享这权利，何况我们？然而我们没有用过这权利，倒凡事忍受，免得基督的福音受到任何拦阻。
refs.text_big5: 若別人在你們身上分享這權利，何況我們？然而我們沒有用過這權利，倒凡事忍受，免得基督的福音受到任何攔阻。
refs.text_en: If others partake of this right over you, should not rather we? Yet we did not use this right, but we bear all things that we may not cause any hindrance to the gospel of Christ.

refs.text_gb: 但这些权利我全没有用过；我写这些话，并非要你们这样待我，因为我宁可死，也不─没有人能使我所夸的落了空。
refs.text_big5: 但這些權利我全沒有用過；我寫這些話，並非要你們這樣待我，因為我寧可死，也不─沒有人能使我所誇的落了空。
refs.text_en: But I myself have not used any of these things; and I have not written these things that it may be so with me; for it is good for me rather to die than-No one shall make my boast void.

refs.text_gb: 使用世物的，要像不浪费使用；因这世界的样子正在逝去。
refs.text_big5: 使用世物的，要像不浪費使用；因這世界的樣子正在逝去。
refs.text_en: And those who use the world as though they did not abuse it; for the fashion of this world is passing away.

verses.text_gb: 我虽从众人得了[Cra]自由，却自愿[Crb]奴役于众人，为要多得人。
verses.text_big5: 我雖從眾人得了[Cra]自由，卻自願[Crb]奴役於眾人，為要多得人。
verses.text_en: For though I am free from all, I have enslaved myself to all that I might gain the more.
verses.text_gb_plain: 我虽从众人得了自由，却自愿奴役于众人，为要多得人。
verses.text_big5_plain: 我雖從眾人得了自由，卻自願奴役於眾人，為要多得人。

refs.text_gb: 我不是自由的么？我不是使徒么？我不是见过我们的主耶稣么？你们不是我在主里所作之工么？
refs.text_big5: 我不是自由的麼？我不是使徒麼？我不是見過我們的主耶穌麼？你們不是我在主裏所作之工麼？
refs.text_en: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?

refs.text_gb: 我说的良心，不是你自己的，乃是别人的。我这自由为什么被别人的良心审判？
refs.text_big5: 我說的良心，不是你自己的，乃是別人的。我這自由為甚麼被別人的良心審判？
refs.text_en: Conscience, I say, not your own, but the other's. For why is my freedom judged by some other conscience?

refs.text_gb: 弟兄们，你们蒙召原是为得自由；只是不可将自由当作放纵肉体的机会，倒要凭着爱互相服事。
refs.text_big5: 弟兄們，你們蒙召原是為得自由；只是不可將自由當作放縱肉體的機會，倒要憑著愛互相服事。
refs.text_en: For you were called for freedom, brothers; only do not turn this freedom into an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.

refs.text_gb: 因为我们不是传自己，乃是传基督耶稣为主，也传自己为耶稣的缘故，作你们的奴仆。
refs.text_big5: 因為我們不是傳自己，乃是傳基督耶穌為主，也傳自己為耶穌的緣故，作你們的奴僕。
refs.text_en: For we do not preach ourselves but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your slaves for Jesus' sake.

verses.text_gb: 向犹太人，我就[Cra]作犹太人，为要[Crb]得犹太人；向[Crc]律法之下的人，我就作律法之下的人，（虽然[Crd]我自己不在律法之下，）为要得律法之下的人；
verses.text_big5: 向猶太人，我就[Cra]作猶太人，為要[Crb]得猶太人；向[Crc]律法之下的人，我就作律法之下的人，（雖然[Crd]我自己不在律法之下，）為要得律法之下的人；
verses.text_en: And to the Jews I became as a Jew in order that I might gain Jews; to those under law, as under law (though I myself am not under law), that I might gain those under law.
verses.text_gb_plain: 向犹太人，我就作犹太人，为要得犹太人；向律法之下的人，我就作律法之下的人，（虽然我自己不在律法之下，）为要得律法之下的人；
verses.text_big5_plain: 向猶太人，我就作猶太人，為要得猶太人；向律法之下的人，我就作律法之下的人，（雖然我自己不在律法之下，）為要得律法之下的人；

refs.text_gb: 保罗有意要他一同出去，只因那些地方的犹太人，就带他去，给他行了割礼，因为他们都知道他父亲是希利尼人。
refs.text_big5: 保羅有意要他一同出去，只因那些地方的猶太人，就帶他去，給他行了割禮，因為他們都知道他父親是希利尼人。
refs.text_en: Paul wanted this one to go forth with him; and he took him and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.

refs.text_gb: 他们听说，你教训一切在外邦的犹太人背弃摩西，对他们说，不要给孩子行割礼，也不要遵行规例。
refs.text_big5: 他們聽說，你教訓一切在外邦的猶太人背棄摩西，對他們說，不要給孩子行割禮，也不要遵行規例。
refs.text_en: And they have been informed concerning you that you are teaching all the Jews throughout the nations apostasy from Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children, nor to walk according to the customs.

refs.text_gb: 众人总会听见你已来了，这可怎么办？
refs.text_big5: 眾人總會聽見你已來了，這可怎麼辦？
refs.text_en: What then is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come.

refs.text_gb: 你就照着我们所告诉你的行吧。我们这里有四个人，都有愿在身；
refs.text_big5: 你就照著我們所告訴你的行罷。我們這裏有四個人，都有願在身；
refs.text_en: Therefore do this that we tell you: We have four men who have a vow on themselves;

refs.text_gb: 你带这些人去，与他们一同行洁净的礼，替他们缴费，叫他们得以剃头，这样，众人就可知道，先前所听说你的事都是虚的，反而你自己却是按规律而行，遵行律法。
refs.text_big5: 你帶這些人去，與他們一同行潔淨的禮，替他們繳費，叫他們得以剃頭，這樣，眾人就可知道，先前所聽說你的事都是虛的，反而你自己卻是按規律而行，遵行律法。
refs.text_en: Take these and be purified with them, and pay their expenses that they may shave their heads. And all will know that there is nothing to the things that they have been informed of concerning you, but that you yourself also walk orderly, keeping the law.

refs.text_gb: 至于信主的外邦人，我们已经写信断定，叫他们自守，远避祭偶像之物和血，并勒死的牲畜与淫乱。
refs.text_big5: 至於信主的外邦人，我們已經寫信斷定，叫他們自守，遠避祭偶像之物和血，並勒死的牲畜與淫亂。
refs.text_en: But concerning the Gentiles who have believed, we have already written, having decided that they should keep themselves from idol sacrifices and blood and anything strangled and fornication.

refs.text_gb: 于是第二天，保罗带着那四个人，与他们一同行了洁净的礼，进了殿，报明洁净的日期满足，只等祭司为他们各人献上供物。
refs.text_big5: 於是第二天，保羅帶著那四個人，與他們一同行了潔淨的禮，進了殿，報明潔淨的日期滿足，只等祭司為他們各人獻上供物。
refs.text_en: Then Paul took the men and on the following day, being purified with them, entered into the temple, giving notice of the completion of the days of the purification, until the offering was offered for each one of them.

refs.text_gb: 那七日将完，从亚西亚来的犹太人，看见保罗在殿里，就耸动了所有的群众，下手拿他，
refs.text_big5: 那七日將完，從亞西亞來的猶太人，看見保羅在殿裏，就聳動了所有的群眾，下手拿他，
refs.text_en: And when the seven days were about to be concluded, the Jews from Asia saw him in the temple and threw all the crowd into confusion; and they laid their hands on him,

refs.text_gb: 喊叫着说，诸位，以色列人哪，请帮忙，这人就是那在各处教训众人反对我们的百姓、律法和这地方的；他又带着希利尼人进殿，污秽了这圣地。
refs.text_big5: 喊叫著說，諸位，以色列人哪，請幫忙，這人就是那在各處教訓眾人反對我們的百姓、律法和這地方的；他又帶著希利尼人進殿，污穢了這聖地。
refs.text_en: Crying out, Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people and the law and this place; and further, he has even brought Greeks into the temple and has profaned this holy place.

refs.text_gb: 或者可以惹动我骨肉之亲妒忌，好救他们一些人。
refs.text_big5: 或者可以惹動我骨肉之親妒忌，好救他們一些人。
refs.text_en: If perhaps I may provoke those of my flesh to jealousy and save some of them.

refs.text_gb: 我们晓得律法上的话，都是对律法以下之人说的，好堵住各人的口，叫普世的人都伏在神的审判之下。
refs.text_big5: 我們曉得律法上的話，都是對律法以下之人說的，好堵住各人的口，叫普世的人都伏在神的審判之下。
refs.text_en: Now we know that whatever things the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, that every mouth may be stopped and all the world may fall under the judgment of God;

refs.text_gb: 我借着律法，已经向律法死了，叫我可以向神活着。
refs.text_big5: 我藉著律法，已經向律法死了，叫我可以向神活著。
refs.text_en: For I through law have died to law that I might live to God.

refs.text_gb: 罪必不能作主管辖你们，因你们不在律法之下，乃在恩典之下。
refs.text_big5: 罪必不能作主管轄你們，因你們不在律法之下，乃在恩典之下。
refs.text_en: For sin will not lord it over you, for you are not under the law but under grace.

verses.text_gb: 向[Cra]律法之外的人，我就[Crb]作律法之外的人，（对神，我不是[Fn1]在律法之外，反而对基督，我是[Fn2]在[Crc]律法之内，）为要得律法之外的人。
verses.text_big5: 向[Cra]律法之外的人，我就[Crb]作律法之外的人，（對神，我不是[Fn1]在律法之外，反而對基督，我是[Fn2]在[Crc]律法之內，）為要得律法之外的人。
verses.text_en: To those without law, as without law (though I am not without law to God but within law to Christ), that I might gain those without law.
verses.text_gb_plain: 向律法之外的人，我就作律法之外的人，（对神，我不是在律法之外，反而对基督，我是在律法之内，）为要得律法之外的人。
verses.text_big5_plain: 向律法之外的人，我就作律法之外的人，（對神，我不是在律法之外，反而對基督，我是在律法之內，）為要得律法之外的人。

footnotes.zh: 即在律法范围、界限之外，因此是没有律法。
footnotes.zh_big5: 即在律法範圍、界限之外，因此是沒有律法。
footnotes.en: 9:21 1 without I.e., outside the sphere, the limit, of law; hence, without law.

footnotes.zh: 即在律法范围、界限之内，因此是服于律法。保罗是以基督为生命，凭基督活着。这活在他里面作生命的基督，带有生命的律，也就是生命的律(罗八2)，管治他，规律他，使他对基督是正当的，合法的，正直的，适当的，所以是在一个更高更好的律法之内，服于这生命的律法。因此，他对神也不是在律法之外，而没有律法。
footnotes.zh_big5: 即在律法範圍、界限之內，因此是服於律法。保羅是以基督為生命，憑基督活著。這活在他裏面作生命的基督，帶有生命的律，也就是生命的律，（羅八2，）管治他，規律他，使他對基督是正當的，合法的，正直的，適當的，所以是在一個更高更好的律法之內，服於這生命的律法。因此，他對神也不是在律法之外，而沒有律法。
footnotes.en: 9:21 2 within I.e., within the sphere, the limit, of law; hence, subject to law. Paul took Christ as his life and lived by Christ. This Christ, who lived in him as life and who has the law of life and is the very law of life (Rom. 8:2), ruled and regulated him that he might be legitimately, legally, rightfully, and duly subject to Christ. Therefore, Paul was within a higher and better law, being subject to the law of life. Hence, he was not outside law and was not without law to God.

refs.text_gb: 凡在律法以外犯了罪的，也必在律法以外灭亡；凡在律法以下犯了罪的，必按律法受审判，
refs.text_big5: 凡在律法以外犯了罪的，也必在律法以外滅亡；凡在律法以下犯了罪的，必按律法受審判，
refs.text_en: For as many as have sinned without the law shall also perish without the law; and as many as have sinned under the law shall be judged by the law

refs.text_gb: 没有律法的外邦人，若顺着本性行律法上的事，他们虽然没有律法，自己就是自己的律法：
refs.text_big5: 沒有律法的外邦人，若順著本性行律法上的事，他們雖然沒有律法，自己就是自己的律法：
refs.text_en: For when Gentiles, who have no law, do by nature the things of the law, these, though they have no law, are a law to themselves,

refs.text_gb: 但与我同去的提多，虽是希利尼人，也没有被勉强受割礼；
refs.text_big5: 但與我同去的提多，雖是希利尼人，也沒有被勉強受割禮；
refs.text_en: But not even Titus, who was with me, though he is a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised;

refs.text_gb: 你们的重担要彼此担当，这样就完全满足了基督的律法。
refs.text_big5: 你們的重擔要彼此擔當，這樣就完全滿足了基督的律法。
refs.text_en: Bear one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ completely.

verses.text_gb: 向软弱的人，我就[Cra]成为软弱的，为要得软弱的人。向众人，我[Fn1]成了[Crb]众人所是的；无论如何，总要[Crc]救些人。
verses.text_big5: 向軟弱的人，我就[Cra]成為軟弱的，為要得軟弱的人。向眾人，我[Fn1]成了[Crb]眾人所是的；無論如何，總要[Crc]救些人。
verses.text_en: To the weak I became weak that I might gain the weak. To all men I have become all things that I might by all means save some.
verses.text_gb_plain: 向软弱的人，我就成为软弱的，为要得软弱的人。向众人，我成了众人所是的；无论如何，总要救些人。
verses.text_big5_plain: 向軟弱的人，我就成為軟弱的，為要得軟弱的人。向眾人，我成了眾人所是的；無論如何，總要救些人。

footnotes.zh: 意指使徒为众人的缘故，调整自己以适应一切的事，也就是适应饮食不同的方式和实行(23)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 意指使徒為眾人的緣故，調整自己以適應一切的事，也就是適應飲食不同的方式和實行。（23。）
footnotes.en: 9:22 1 become This means that the apostle adapted himself to all things, that is, to different ways of eating and practice (v. 23), for the sake of all men.

refs.text_gb: 我们刚强的人，应该担代不刚强之人的软弱，不求自己的喜悦。
refs.text_big5: 我們剛強的人，應該擔代不剛強之人的軟弱，不求自己的喜悅。
refs.text_en: But we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those who are weak and not to please ourselves.

refs.text_gb: 有谁软弱，我不软弱？有谁绊跌，我不焦急？
refs.text_big5: 有誰軟弱，我不軟弱？有誰絆跌，我不焦急？
refs.text_en: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is stumbled, and I myself do not burn?

refs.text_gb: 就好像我也凡事叫众人喜悦，不寻求自己的益处，只寻求多人的益处，叫他们可以得救。
refs.text_big5: 就好像我也凡事叫眾人喜悅，不尋求自己的益處，只尋求多人的益處，叫他們可以得救。
refs.text_en: Even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own advantage but that of the many, that they may be saved.

refs.text_gb: 或者可以惹动我骨肉之亲妒忌，好救他们一些人。
refs.text_big5: 或者可以惹動我骨肉之親妒忌，好救他們一些人。
refs.text_en: If perhaps I may provoke those of my flesh to jealousy and save some of them.

refs.text_gb: 况且你这作妻子的，怎么知道能不能救你的丈夫？你这作丈夫的，怎么知道能不能救你的妻子？
refs.text_big5: 況且你這作妻子的，怎麼知道能不能救你的丈夫？你這作丈夫的，怎麼知道能不能救你的妻子？
refs.text_en: For how do you know, O wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, O husband, whether you will save your wife?

verses.text_gb: 凡我所行的，都是为福音的缘故，为要与人[Fn1][Cra]同享这福音。
verses.text_big5: 凡我所行的，都是為福音的緣故，為要與人[Fn1][Cra]同享這福音。
verses.text_en: And I do all things for the sake of the gospel that I may become a fellow partaker of it.
verses.text_gb_plain: 凡我所行的，都是为福音的缘故，为要与人同享这福音。
verses.text_big5_plain: 凡我所行的，都是為福音的緣故，為要與人同享這福音。

footnotes.zh: 直译，作这福音的同享者(或共同有分者，合作者，合伙者)。使徒不仅是同享者、共同分享者，享受福音；也是合作者、合伙者，为福音劳苦。但在这里，他是指对福音的享受，因此，我们在经文里译为“同享这福音。”
footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，作這福音的同享者（或共同有分者，合作者，合夥者）。使徒不僅是同享者、共同分享者，享受福音；也是合作者、合夥者，為福音勞苦。但在這裏，他是指對福音的享受，因此，我們在經文裏譯為“同享這福音。”
footnotes.en: 9:23 1 fellow Or, joint participant, cooperator, copartner. The apostle was not only a fellow partaker, a joint participant, enjoying the gospel but also a cooperator, a copartner, laboring for the gospel. However, here he referred to the enjoyment of the gospel. Hence, this word is rendered fellow partaker in the text.

refs.text_gb: 我为你们众人有这样的想法，原是应当的，因为你们有我在你们心里，无论我在捆锁之中，或在辩护、证实福音的时候，你们众人都与我同享恩典。
refs.text_big5: 我為你們眾人有這樣的想法，原是應當的，因為你們有我在你們心裏，無論我在捆鎖之中，或在辯護、證實福音的時候，你們眾人都與我同享恩典。
refs.text_en: Even as it is right for me to think this concerning you all because you have me in your heart, since both in my bonds and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel you are all fellow partakers with me of grace.

verses.text_gb: 岂不知在[Cra]场上[Fn1]赛跑的都跑，但得[Fn2][Crb]奖赏的只有一人？你们应当这样[Crc]跑，好叫你们得着奖赏。
verses.text_big5: 豈不知在[Cra]場上[Fn1]賽跑的都跑，但得[Fn2][Crb]獎賞的只有一人？你們應當這樣[Crc]跑，好叫你們得著獎賞。
verses.text_en: Do you not know that those who run on a racecourse all run, but one receives the prize? Run in this way, that you may lay hold.
verses.text_gb_plain: 岂不知在场上赛跑的都跑，但得奖赏的只有一人？你们应当这样跑，好叫你们得着奖赏。
verses.text_big5_plain: 豈不知在場上賽跑的都跑，但得獎賞的只有一人？你們應當這樣跑，好叫你們得著獎賞。

footnotes.zh: 这启示基督徒的生活，乃是一场赛跑，我们必须跑得成功。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這啟示基督徒的生活，乃是一場賽跑，我們必須跑得成功。
footnotes.en: 9:24 1 run This reveals that the Christian life is a race that we must run successfully.

footnotes.zh: 即一种作为激励的赏赐。见17注1。
footnotes.zh_big5: 即一種作為激勵的賞賜。見17註1。
footnotes.en: 9:24 2 prize I.e., a reward as an incentive. See note 1 Cor. 9:17 1 .

refs.text_gb: 我却不以性命为念，也不看为宝贵，只要行完我的路程，成就我从主耶稣所领受的职事，郑重见证神恩典的福音。
refs.text_big5: 我卻不以性命為念，也不看為寶貴，只要行完我的路程，成就我從主耶穌所領受的職事，鄭重見證神恩典的福音。
refs.text_en: But I consider my life of no account as if precious to myself, in order that I may finish my course and the ministry which I have received from the Lord Jesus to solemnly testify of the gospel of the grace of God.

refs.text_gb: 那美好的仗我已经打过了，当跑的赛程我已经跑尽了，当守的信仰我已经守住了；
refs.text_big5: 那美好的仗我已經打過了，當跑的賽程我已經跑盡了，當守的信仰我已經守住了；
refs.text_en: I have fought the good fight; I have finished the course; I have kept the faith.

refs.text_gb: 所以，我们既有这许多的见证人，如同云彩围着我们，就当脱去各样的重担，和容易缠累我们的罪，凭着忍耐奔那摆在我们前头的赛程，
refs.text_big5: 所以，我們既有這許多的見證人，如同雲彩圍著我們，就當脫去各樣的重擔，和容易纏累我們的罪，憑著忍耐奔那擺在我們前頭的賽程，

footnotes.zh: 指当时为运动竞赛，用树叶所作之圆冠。不能坏的华冠，就是主所要赏给赢得赛跑之得胜圣徒的，乃是在救恩之外另加上的赏赐(见来十35注1)。我们这些主的信徒，都已借信接受了祂的救恩，这是一定永定的。但我们将来能否得祂的赏赐，乃在于我们如何奔跑赛程。在本章这里，使徒正在场上奔跑(26)；在他晚期的一封书信，腓立比书里，他还在奔跑(腓三14)；直到提后四6～8，他奔跑到了最后一刻，才有把握会在主显现时得祂的赏赐。在这奖赏的光中，使徒嘱咐哥林多信徒，要跑这一场赛跑，使他们能得着赏赐(24)。
footnotes.en: 9:25 1 crown A chaplet made of leaves for the athletic contests at that time. The incorruptible crown, which the Lord will award to His overcoming saints who win the race, is a reward in addition to salvation (see note Heb. 10:35 1 ). We, His believers, have all received His salvation through faith in Him. This has been settled once for all. But whether we will be rewarded by Him depends on how we run the race. Here, in this chapter, the apostle was running the course (v. 26). In Philippians, one of his last Epistles, he was still running (Phil. 3:14). It was not until the last moment of his running, in 2 Tim. 4:6-8, that he had the assurance that he would be rewarded by the Lord at His appearing. In view of this prize the apostle charged the Corinthian believers to run the race that they might obtain the reward (v. 24).

footnotes.zh: 原文意，把眼睛以下的脸面打得又黑又青。这不像禁欲主义者苦待身体，也不像智慧派认为身体是邪恶的。这是要治服身体，使其成为被征服的俘虏，像奴隶一样服事我们，好成就我们神圣的目的。这相当于治死我们在地上的肢体(西三5)，并治死身体的行为(罗八13)，不让我们的身体用为放纵情欲，除了神看为圣的事，也不凭自己作什么。哥林多人纵情淫乱，滥用他们的身体，不顾神的殿(六19)，并且任意吃祭偶像之物，不顾软弱的信徒(八9～13)。

footnotes.en: 9:27 1 buffet The Greek word means to beat the face under the eye black and blue. This is not to ill-treat the body, as in asceticism, nor to consider the body evil, as in Gnosticism. This is to subdue the body and make it a conquered captive to serve us as a slave for fulfilling our holy purpose. This is equivalent to putting to death our earthly members (Col. 3:5) and putting to death the practices of the body (Rom. 8:13), not allowing our body to be used for the indulgence of lust or doing anything on our own except what is holy to God. The Corinthians misused their body by indulgence in fornication, not caring for God's temple (1 Cor. 6:19), and in the unrestrained eating of things sacrificed to idols, not caring for weak believers (1 Cor. 8:9-13).

footnotes.zh: 根据24～27节经文，这是指传讲赏赐，以激励奔跑的基督徒。赏赐与国度有关；国度的实现，要成为赢得基督徒赛跑得胜圣徒的赏赐。见来十二28注1。
footnotes.zh_big5: 根據24～27節經文，這是指傳講賞賜，以激勵奔跑的基督徒。賞賜與國度有關；國度的實現，要成為贏得基督徒賽跑得勝聖徒的賞賜。見來十二28註1。
footnotes.en: 9:27 4 preached According to the context of vv. 24-27, this refers to the preaching of the reward as an incentive to the Christian runners. This is related to the kingdom, the manifestation of which will be a reward to the overcoming saints who have won the Christian race. See note Heb. 12:28 1 .

footnotes.zh: 或，不合格，被弃绝。亦即不配得奖赏。使徒必定是借着相信基督，靠恩得救的。不仅如此，他也蒙召作使徒，以完成神新约的经纶。然而，他在这里却极其儆醒的奔跑他的赛程(徒二十24)，治服自己的身体，以适于他神圣的目的，使他在基督的审判台前，不致不蒙称许，并被弃绝(林后五10)，不配得着要来国度的赏赐。见太七21～23与二五11～12。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，不合格，被棄絕。亦即不配得獎賞。使徒必定是藉著相信基督，靠恩得救的。不僅如此，他也蒙召作使徒，以完成神新約的經綸。然而，他在這裏卻極其儆醒的奔跑他的賽程，（徒二十24，）治服自己的身體，以適於他神聖的目的，使他在基督的審判臺前，不致不蒙稱許，並被棄絕，（林後五10，）不配得著要來國度的賞賜。見太七21～23與二五11～12。
footnotes.en: 9:27 5 disapproved Or, disqualified, rejected; i.e., unworthy of the prize. The apostle was surely saved by grace through faith in Christ. Not only so, he was called to be an apostle to carry out God's New Testament economy. Nonetheless, here he was very much on the alert to run his course (Acts 20:24) by subduing his body to serve his holy purpose, that he might not be disapproved and rejected at the judgment seat of Christ (2 Cor. 5:10) and be found unworthy of the reward of the coming kingdom. See Matt. 7:21-23; 25:11-12.

footnotes.en: 10:1 4 cloud The cloud that covered the children of Israel typifies the Spirit of God, who is with the New Testament believers. Immediately after the New Testament believers take Christ as their Passover (1 Cor. 5:7), the Spirit of God comes to be with them and lead them to run the Christian race, just as the pillar of cloud led the children of Israel (Exo. 13:21-22; 14:19-20).

refs.text_en: And Jehovah went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them on the way and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, that they might go by day and by night.

refs.text_gb: 日间云柱，夜间火柱，总不离开百姓的面前。
refs.text_big5: 日間雲柱，夜間火柱，總不離開百姓的面前。
refs.text_en: Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night departed from before the people.

refs.text_gb: 在以色列营前行走的神的使者，转到他们后边行走；云柱也从他们前边转到他们后边立住。
refs.text_big5: 在以色列營前行走的神的使者，轉到他們後邊行走；雲柱也從他們前邊轉到他們後邊立住。
refs.text_en: And the Angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud moved from before them and stood behind them.

refs.text_gb: 在埃及营和以色列营之间有云柱，一边黑暗，一边发光；终夜双方不得相近。
refs.text_big5: 在埃及營和以色列營之間有雲柱，一邊黑暗，一邊發光；終夜雙方不得相近。
refs.text_en: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel. And the cloud was there with the darkness, yet it gave light by night to them. Thus one did not come near the other all night.

refs.text_gb: 摩西向海伸手，耶和华便用强大的东风，使海水一夜退去，叫海成了干地；水就分开了。
refs.text_big5: 摩西向海伸手，耶和華便用強大的東風，使海水一夜退去，叫海成了乾地；水就分開了。
refs.text_en: And when Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, Jehovah caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all the night and made the sea dry land; and the waters were divided.

refs.text_gb: 以色列人下到海中，走在干地上，水在他们的左右作了墙垣。
refs.text_big5: 以色列人下到海中，走在乾地上，水在他們的左右作了牆垣。
refs.text_en: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.

refs.text_gb: 以色列人却在海中干地上走过；水在他们的左右作了墙垣。
refs.text_big5: 以色列人卻在海中乾地上走過；水在他們的左右作了牆垣。
refs.text_en: But the children of Israel walked on dry land through the midst of the sea, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.

verses.text_gb: 都[Fn1]在云里，也在海里，[Fn2][Cra]受浸[Fn3]归了摩西；
verses.text_big5: 都[Fn1]在雲裏，也在海裏，[Fn2][Cra]受浸[Fn3]歸了摩西；
verses.text_en: And all were baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
verses.text_gb_plain: 都在云里，也在海里，受浸归了摩西；
verses.text_big5_plain: 都在雲裏，也在海裏，受浸歸了摩西；

footnotes.zh: 在云里，表征在那灵里。在海里，指在水里。新约信徒是在水里，并在那灵里受浸的(太三11，徒一5，林前十二13)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 在雲裏，表徵在那靈裏。在海裏，指在水裏。新約信徒是在水裏，並在那靈裏受浸的。（太三11，徒一5，林前十二13。）
footnotes.en: 10:2 1 baptized The passing of the children of Israel through the Red Sea (Exo. 14:21-30) typifies the baptism of the New Testament believers (Rom. 6:4).

footnotes.zh: 以色列人的过红海(出十四21～30)，预表新约信徒的受浸(罗六4)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 以色列人的過紅海，（出十四21～30，）豫表新約信徒的受浸。（羅六4。）
footnotes.en: 10:2 2 unto The children of Israel were baptized unto Moses to begin the holy race for the fulfilling of God's purpose, that is, to enter into the good land and build the temple, that God might have a kingdom with an expression of Himself on the earth. This typifies the baptizing of the New Testament believers into Christ (Gal. 3:27) that God may have His kingdom with the church as His expression on the earth.

footnotes.zh: 以色列人受浸归了摩西，开始神圣的赛程，以成就神的定旨，就是进入美地，并建造圣殿，使神可以得着国度，在地上有祂自己的彰显。这预表新约信徒是浸入基督(加三27)，使神能得着祂的国，有召会在地上作祂的彰显。
footnotes.zh_big5: 以色列人受浸歸了摩西，開始神聖的賽程，以成就神的定旨，就是進入美地，並建造聖殿，使神可以得著國度，在地上有祂自己的彰顯。這豫表新約信徒是浸入基督，（加三27，）使神能得著祂的國，有召會在地上作祂的彰顯。
footnotes.en: 10:2 3 in In the cloud signifies in the Spirit, and in the sea denotes in the water. The New Testament believers were baptized in the water and in the Spirit (Matt. 3:11; Acts 1:5; 1 Cor. 12:13).

refs.text_gb: 岂不知我们这浸入基督耶稣的人，是浸入祂的死么？
refs.text_big5: 豈不知我們這浸入基督耶穌的人，是浸入祂的死麼？
refs.text_en: Or are you ignorant that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus have been baptized into His death?

refs.text_gb: 你们凡浸入基督的，都已经穿上了基督。
refs.text_big5: 你們凡浸入基督的，都已經穿上了基督。
refs.text_en: For as many as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

verses.text_gb: 并且都吃了一样的[Fn1]灵[Cra]食，
verses.text_big5: 並且都喫了一樣的[Fn1]靈[Cra]食，
verses.text_en: And all ate the same spiritual food,
verses.text_gb_plain: 并且都吃了一样的灵食，
verses.text_big5_plain: 並且都喫了一樣的靈食，

footnotes.zh: 指吗哪(出十六14～18)，预表基督为着基督徒的旅程，作我们每日生命的供应(约六31～35)。我们信徒都该吃一样的灵食，不该吃基督之外的任何东西。
footnotes.zh_big5: 指嗎哪，（出十六14～18，）豫表基督為著基督徒的旅程，作我們每日生命的供應。（約六31～35。）我們信徒都該喫一樣的靈食，不該喫基督之外的任何東西。
footnotes.en: 10:3 1 spiritual Referring to manna (Exo. 16:14-18), typifying Christ as our daily life supply (John 6:31-35) for the Christian journey. We believers should all eat the same spiritual food and should not eat anything other than Christ.

refs.text_gb: 耶和华对摩西说，我要将粮食从天降给你们。百姓可以出去，每天收取当天的分，我好试验他们遵不遵行我的法度。
refs.text_big5: 耶和華對摩西說，我要將糧食從天降給你們。百姓可以出去，每天收取當天的分，我好試驗他們遵不遵行我的法度。
refs.text_en: Then Jehovah said to Moses, I will now rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a day's portion every day, that I may test them, whether or not they will walk in My law.

refs.text_gb: 露水上升之后，不料，旷野的地面上有细小的圆物，细小如地上的霜。
refs.text_big5: 露水上升之後，不料，曠野的地面上有細小的圓物，細小如地上的霜。
refs.text_en: And when the layer of dew lifted, there upon the surface of the wilderness were fine round flakes, fine as the frost on the earth.

refs.text_gb: 以色列人看见，不知道是什么，就彼此对问说，这是什么？摩西对他们说，这就是耶和华给你们吃的食物。
refs.text_big5: 以色列人看見，不知道是甚麼，就彼此對問說，這是甚麼？摩西對他們說，這就是耶和華給你們喫的食物。
refs.text_en: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another, What is it? For they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, It is the bread which Jehovah has given you to eat.

refs.text_gb: 以色列人吃吗哪共四十年，直到进了有人居住之地，就是迦南地的境界。
refs.text_big5: 以色列人喫嗎哪共四十年，直到進了有人居住之地，就是迦南地的境界。
refs.text_en: And the children of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to inhabitable land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.

refs.text_gb: 现在我们的胃口都没有了，我们眼前除了这吗哪以外，什么也没有。
refs.text_big5: 現在我們的胃口都沒有了，我們眼前除了這嗎哪以外，甚麼也沒有。
refs.text_en: But now our appetite has gone; there is nothing at all but this manna to look at.

refs.text_gb: 这吗哪仿佛芫荽子，样子好像珍珠。
refs.text_big5: 這嗎哪彷彿芫荽子，樣子好像珍珠。
refs.text_en: Now the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium.

refs.text_gb: 百姓周围行走，把吗哪收起来，或用磨碾，或用臼捣，在锅里煮，又作成饼；滋味好像烤的油饼。
refs.text_big5: 百姓周圍行走，把嗎哪收起來，或用磨碾，或用臼搗，在鍋裏煮，又作成餅；滋味好像烤的油餅。
refs.text_en: The people went about and gathered it and ground it between two millstones or beat it in a mortar; then they boiled it in pots and made cakes of it; and its taste was like the taste of cakes baked in oil.

refs.text_gb: 夜间露水降在营中的时候，吗哪也随着降下。
refs.text_big5: 夜間露水降在營中的時候，嗎哪也隨著降下。
refs.text_en: And when the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna would fall with it.

refs.text_gb: 降吗哪像雨给他们吃，将天上的粮食赐给他们。
refs.text_big5: 降嗎哪像雨給他們喫，將天上的糧食賜給他們。
refs.text_en: And He rained down upon them manna to eat / And gave them the food of heaven.

refs.text_gb: 人吃大能者的食物；祂差下粮食，使他们饱足。
refs.text_big5: 人喫大能者的食物；祂差下糧食，使他們飽足。
refs.text_en: Man ate the bread of the mighty; / He sent them full provision.

refs.text_gb: 我们的祖宗在旷野吃过吗哪，如经上所记：“祂把那从天上来的粮赐给他们吃。”
refs.text_big5: 我們的祖宗在曠野喫過嗎哪，如經上所記：“祂把那從天上來的糧賜給他們喫。”
refs.text_en: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written, "He gave them bread out of heaven to eat."

verses.text_gb: 也都喝了一样的[Fn1]灵[Cra]水；所喝的是出于随行的[Fn2]灵磐石，那磐石就是基督。
verses.text_big5: 也都喝了一樣的[Fn1]靈[Cra]水；所喝的是出於隨行的[Fn2]靈磐石，那磐石就是基督。
verses.text_en: And all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank of a spiritual rock which followed them, and the rock was Christ.
verses.text_gb_plain: 也都喝了一样的灵水；所喝的是出于随行的灵磐石，那磐石就是基督。
verses.text_big5_plain: 也都喝了一樣的靈水；所喝的是出於隨行的靈磐石，那磐石就是基督。

footnotes.zh: 指流自裂开磐石的活水(出十七6)，预表那流自钉死十架而复活之基督的灵，作我们包罗万有的水(约七37～39，林前十二13)。为着奔跑赛程，我们都该喝一样的灵水，不该喝这包罗万有之灵以外的任何东西。
footnotes.zh_big5: 指流自裂開磐石的活水，（出十七6，）豫表那流自釘死十架而復活之基督的靈，作我們包羅萬有的水。（約七37～39，林前十二13。）為著奔跑賽程，我們都該喝一樣的靈水，不該喝這包羅萬有之靈以外的任何東西。
footnotes.en: 10:4 1 spiritual Referring to the living water that flowed out of the cleft rock (Exo. 17:6), typifying the Spirit, who flowed out of the crucified and resurrected Christ, as our all-inclusive drink (John 7:37-39; 1 Cor. 12:13). For our running of the race we should all drink the same spiritual drink and should not drink anything other than the all-inclusive Spirit.

footnotes.zh: 为着神的选民被击打、裂开、流出活水的磐石(出十七6)，乃是物质的磐石；但使徒称之为灵磐石，因它预表那被神击打、裂开，流出生命的水(约十九34)，以解信徒干渴的基督。因此使徒说，那磐石就是基督。它既是表征基督的灵磐石，就能随着以色列人。这指明作真磐石的基督，乃是随着祂的信徒。
footnotes.zh_big5: 為著神的選民被擊打、裂開、流出活水的磐石，（出十七6，）乃是物質的磐石；但使徒稱之為靈磐石，因它豫表那被神擊打、裂開，流出生命的水，（約十九34，）以解信徒乾渴的基督。因此使徒說，那磐石就是基督。它既是表徵基督的靈磐石，就能隨著以色列人。這指明作真磐石的基督，乃是隨著祂的信徒。
footnotes.en: 10:4 2 spiritual The rock that was smitten and cleft to flow out the living water for God's chosen people (Exo. 17:6) was a physical rock. Yet the apostle called it a spiritual rock because it typified Christ, who was smitten and cleft by God to flow out the water of life (John 19:34) to satisfy the thirst of His believers. Hence, the apostle said that the rock was Christ. Since it was a spiritual rock signifying Christ, it was able to follow the children of Israel. This indicates that Christ as the real rock is following His believers.

refs.text_gb: 我必在何烈的磐石那里，站在你面前；你要击打磐石，就必有水从磐石流出来，使百姓可以喝。摩西就在以色列的长老眼前这样行了。
refs.text_big5: 我必在何烈的磐石那裏，站在你面前；你要擊打磐石，就必有水從磐石流出來，使百姓可以喝。摩西就在以色列的長老眼前這樣行了。
refs.text_en: I will be standing before you there upon the rock in Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it so that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.

refs.text_gb: 摩西、亚伦就招聚会众到磐石前；摩西对他们说，你们这些背叛的人听我说，我们要为你们使水从这磐石中流出来么？
refs.text_big5: 摩西、亞倫就招聚會眾到磐石前；摩西對他們說，你們這些背叛的人聽我說，我們要為你們使水從這磐石中流出來麼？
refs.text_en: And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said to them, Listen now, you rebels: Shall we bring forth water for you out of this rock?

refs.text_gb: 祂在旷野裂开磐石，多多地给他们水喝，如从深渊而出。
refs.text_big5: 祂在曠野裂開磐石，多多的給他們水喝，如從深淵而出。
refs.text_en: He split rocks in the wilderness / And gave them abundant drink, as from the depths.

refs.text_gb: 祂使水从磐石涌出，叫水如江河流下。
refs.text_big5: 祂使水從磐石湧出，叫水如江河流下。
refs.text_en: He also brought forth streams from the rock / And made water run down like rivers.

verses.text_gb: 但他们大多数的人，神并不喜悦，因此他们[Fn1][Cra]倒毙在旷野。
verses.text_big5: 但他們大多數的人，神並不喜悅，因此他們[Fn1][Cra]倒斃在曠野。
verses.text_en: But with most of them God was not well pleased, for they were strewn along in the wilderness.
verses.text_gb_plain: 但他们大多数的人，神并不喜悦，因此他们倒毙在旷野。
verses.text_big5_plain: 但他們大多數的人，神並不喜悅，因此他們倒斃在曠野。

footnotes.zh: 即被杀倒地。这是指民十四16、29说的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 即被殺倒地。這是指民十四16、29說的。
footnotes.en: 10:5 1 strewn I.e., laid low on the ground by being slain. This refers to Num. 14:16, 29.

refs.text_gb: 我们也不要行淫，像他们有些人行的，一天就倒毙了二万三千人。
refs.text_big5: 我們也不要行淫，像他們有些人行的，一天就倒斃了二萬三千人。
refs.text_en: Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and there fell in one day twenty-three thousand.

refs.text_gb: 我们也不要试探基督，像他们有些人试探的，就被蛇所灭。
refs.text_big5: 我們也不要試探基督，像他們有些人試探的，就被蛇所滅。
refs.text_en: Neither let us test Christ, as some of them tested Him and were destroyed by the serpents.

refs.text_gb: 你们也不要发怨言，像他们有些人发的，就被灭命的所灭。
refs.text_big5: 你們也不要發怨言，像他們有些人發的，就被滅命的所滅。
refs.text_en: Neither murmur, just as some of them murmured and perished by the destroyer.

refs.text_gb: 你们的尸首必倒在这旷野，并且你们中间凡被数点的，就是按所计算的数目，从二十岁以上，向我发过怨言的，
refs.text_big5: 你們的屍首必倒在這曠野，並且你們中間凡被數點的，就是按所計算的數目，從二十歲以上，向我發過怨言的，
refs.text_en: Your corpses shall fall in this wilderness, and none of you who were numbered, according to the number you counted from twenty years old and upward, who have murmured against Me,

refs.text_gb: 我耶和华说了，我必要这样待这一切聚集攻击我的恶会众；他们必在这旷野消灭，在这里死亡。
refs.text_big5: 我耶和華說了，我必要這樣待這一切聚集攻擊我的惡會眾；他們必在這曠野消滅，在這裏死亡。
refs.text_en: I, Jehovah, have spoken; surely I will do this to all this evil assembly who are gathered together against Me. In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.

refs.text_gb: 因为耶和华曾论到他们说，他们必要死在旷野。除了耶孚尼的儿子迦勒和嫩的儿子约书亚以外，连一个人也没有存留。
refs.text_big5: 因為耶和華曾論到他們說，他們必要死在曠野。除了耶孚尼的兒子迦勒和嫩的兒子約書亞以外，連一個人也沒有存留。
refs.text_en: For Jehovah had said of them, They shall surely die in the wilderness. And not one of them was left, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun.

refs.text_gb: 所以祂对他们举手起誓，必叫他们倒在旷野，
refs.text_big5: 所以祂對他們舉手起誓，必叫他們倒在曠野，
refs.text_en: Therefore He lifted up His hand and swore to them / That He would make them fall in the wilderness,

refs.text_gb: 神四十年之久，又厌烦了谁？岂不是那些犯罪，尸首倒在旷野的人么？
refs.text_big5: 神四十年之久，又厭煩了誰？豈不是那些犯罪，屍首倒在曠野的人麼？
refs.text_en: And with whom was He displeased for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose carcasses fell in the wilderness?

verses.text_gb: 这些事都是[Fn1]我们的[Fn2][Cra]鉴戒，叫我们不作贪恋恶事的人，像他们那样[Crb]贪恋。
verses.text_big5: 這些事都是[Fn1]我們的[Fn2][Cra]鑑戒，叫我們不作貪戀惡事的人，像他們那樣[Crb]貪戀。
verses.text_en: Now these things occurred as examples to us, that we should not be ones who lust after evil things, even as they also lusted.
verses.text_gb_plain: 这些事都是我们的鉴戒，叫我们不作贪恋恶事的人，像他们那样贪恋。
verses.text_big5_plain: 這些事都是我們的鑑戒，叫我們不作貪戀惡事的人，像他們那樣貪戀。

footnotes.zh: 在奔跑基督徒的赛程上，使徒把自己与众信徒包括在一起。
footnotes.zh_big5: 在奔跑基督徒的賽程上，使徒把自己與眾信徒包括在一起。
footnotes.en: 10:6 1 examples Lit., types (so also in v. 11); i.e., figures of facts or of spiritual truths. This book takes the history of the children of Israel in the Old Testament as a type of the New Testament believers. In 1 Cor. 5:7-8 the believers experienced Christ as their Passover and began to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Here in this chapter they are baptized unto their Moses (Christ), passing through their Red Sea (the death of Christ). They are now eating the spiritual food and drinking the spiritual drink that they might take their journey (the Christian race) toward their good land (the all-inclusive Christ). Also, they are warned here (v. 11) not to repeat the history of the children of Israel in doing evil against God, as illustrated in vv. 6-11. The goal of God's calling of the children of Israel was that they would enter into the promised land to enjoy its riches so that they might establish God's kingdom and be God's expression on earth. However, although all Israel was redeemed through the Passover, delivered out of the Egyptian tyranny, and brought to the mountain of God to receive the revelation of God's dwelling place, the tabernacle, nearly all fell and died in the wilderness, failing to reach this goal (Heb. 3:7-19) because of their evildoings and unbelief. Only Caleb and Joshua reached the goal and entered into the good land (Num. 14:27-30). This signifies that although we have been redeemed through Christ, delivered out of Satan's bondage, and brought into the revelation of God's economy, we may yet fail to reach the goal of God's calling, that is, to enter into the possession of our good land, Christ (Phil. 3:12-14), and enjoy His riches for the kingdom of God that we may be His expression in the present age and participate in the fullest enjoyment of Christ in the kingdom age (Matt. 25:21, 23). This should be a solemn warning to all New Testament believers. It was especially applicable to the Corinthians, who were in danger of repeating the failure of the children of Israel in the wilderness.
